cubes.name: AssetCategories
cubes.title: Asset Categories
cubes.description: Lookup table of all asset type labels. Type classify assets by type using snake_case IDs mapped to human-readable names - cloud (e.g., "virtual_machine" -> "Virtual Machine", "cloud_firewall" -> "Cloud Firewall", "dns_server" -> "DNS Server", "storage_bucket" -> "Storage Bucket"), network (e.g., "router" -> "Router", "switch" -> "Switch", "load_balancer" -> "Load Balancer"), and IoT/endpoint (e.g., "camera" -> "Camera", "printer" -> "Printer", "bare_metal_server" -> "Bare-Metal Server"). An asset can have multiple Types. Use this cube to list available categories and their display names. Example queries: "what types exist", "list all asset types", "show me all firewall assets", "how many virtual machines do I have", or populating a type filter dropdown.

cubes.name: AssetDetailsOnly
cubes.title: Asset Details Only
cubes.description: Asset-only inventory cube with one row per unique asset (no insight row expansion). Exposes common normalised asset attributes such as name, provider, region/location, OS/version, vendor/model, IP/MAC addresses, categories, taxonomy hierarchy, tags, lifecycle fields, and discovery status signals. Use this cube only for tag-introspection or asset-registry-lookup queries that do not enumerate assets by attribute, for example "find assets by tag key/value", "list all available tag keys", "count assets by provider", or "show devices by taxonomy type". Do NOT use this cube for general asset enumeration such as "list Windows servers", "show managed devices by region", or "find assets by OS" - use AssetDetailsAggV1 for those. Do NOT use this cube when the query requires insight-specific fields (indicator/state/severity/confidence) or provider/interface expanded raw attributes; use AssetDetailsAggV1 in that case. Time dimension: default to updated_at scoped to the last 7 days from now (to the minute); if the user specifies a time range - for example "in the last 3 hours", "over the past 2 days", or "not in the last 3 days" - apply those constraints instead, as user-specified time always takes priority over the default.

cubes.name: AssetDetails_ch
cubes.title: Asset Details
cubes.description: Primary detail asset-and-insight cube combining normalised asset attributes, active insight rows, and 7-day user logon counts. Grain is one row per asset-insight combination, so a single asset can produce multiple rows when it has multiple active insights. Each row exposes: (1) common asset context such as provider, region, OS, vendor, model, categories, taxonomy, tags, lifecycle timestamps, and discovery status fields; (2) one active insight record with classification, indicator, rule ID, confidence, severity, state, and sub-classification; and (3) asset-level recent user activity counts. Use this cube when a query needs both asset context and per-insight detail, for example "show active insights by provider and severity", "list assets with registration issues by region", or "break down violated insights by taxonomy type and confidence". This cube and AssetInsightOnlyV1 both have one insight per row, so both can correctly GROUP BY or break down by insight dimensions (classification, sub-classification, indicator, confidence, severity, state); prefer this cube when the breakdown also groups by or returns asset attributes (provider, OS, region, vendor, taxonomy), and prefer AssetInsightOnlyV1 for lightweight insight-only breakdowns with little or no asset context. For asset inventory with rolled-up insight arrays - one row per asset, insight fields used only for filtering - prefer AssetDetailsAggV1; do NOT use AssetDetailsAggV1 to group by an insight dimension, as its insight fields are per-asset arrays. Time dimension: default to updated_at scoped to the last 7 days from now (to the minute); if the user specifies a time range - for example "in the last 3 hours", "over the past 2 days", or "not in the last 3 days" - apply those constraints instead, as user-specified time always takes priority over the default.

cubes.name: AssetDetails_ch_agg
cubes.title: Asset Details Agg
cubes.description: Primary aggregated asset cube combining normalised asset attributes, rolled-up insight arrays, and 7-day user logon summaries. Grain is one row per asset (CQID). Each row exposes: (1) common asset fields - name, OS, vendor, model, IP/MAC addresses, categories, location, managed status, first/last seen, tags, and source table; (2) aggregated security insight context - insight types, indicators, confidence levels, severities, states, sub-classifications, and pre-computed composite keys such as insight_types_confidence_levels; and (3) user activity rollups - distinct user count plus user-to-name/action/timestamp maps. This is the default workhorse cube for all general asset queries - use it with or without insight filtering. Use for any asset enumeration or attribute-based lookup, for example "list all Windows servers", "show all managed Linux devices by region", "list managed assets by OS and vendor", "find assets by name or IP", as well as insight-filtered analytics such as "show assets with active security insights by OS" or "list devices with recent user activity and violations". Insight fields here (classification, sub-classification, indicator, confidence, severity, state) are stored as per-asset arrays: use them to FILTER assets that have a given insight, but NOT to GROUP or break down BY an insight value - grouping operates on the whole array, not individual values, and produces incorrect counts. For any query that groups by, breaks down by, or counts WITHIN an insight dimension (e.g. "zombie assets by sub-classification", "count insights by severity", "breakdown by classification and confidence"), use AssetInsightOnlyV1 (pure insight breakdown, minimal asset context) or AssetDetailsV1 (one row per asset-insight, when the breakdown also groups by or returns asset attributes such as provider, OS, region, or vendor) instead. For interface- or provider-specific raw fields, use the corresponding *_agg_expanded cubes. Time dimension: default to updated_at scoped to the last 7 days from now (to the minute); if the user specifies a time range - for example "in the last 3 hours", "over the past 2 days", or "not in the last 3 days" - apply those constraints instead, as user-specified time always takes priority over the default.

cubes.name: AssetDiscoveryStatus
cubes.title: Asset Discovery Status
cubes.description: Device discovery-status cube with one row per asset. Exposes discovery and network collection health fields such as device IP/name/type, reachability results, SNMP or CLI or SDN credential and collection statuses, fingerprinting outcomes, discovery timestamps, overall status, discovery service identifiers, and device-type confidence signals. Use this cube when a query focuses on operational discovery health rather than general asset inventory or insight analytics, for example "show unreachable devices by type", "list assets with failed SNMP credentials", "find devices with low type-identification confidence", or "track SDN collection failures by source job". Prefer this cube over broader asset cube when the question is primarily about discovery workflow status because it keeps the surface focused on discovery-specific fields.

cubes.name: AssetInsight
cubes.title: Asset Insight
cubes.description: Security and compliance insight cube enriched with dictionary labels for insight type, indicator, and location. Grain is detailed and time-aware: rows represent indicator/rule findings per asset over time windows, with latest values selected per grouped keys in the query logic. Use this cube for insight-centric analysis such as "show active violations by severity", "list findings by indicator and provider", "track acknowledged vs unacknowledged insights", or "break down insights by asset type/location". Prefer this cube when the question is primarily about insight lifecycle, confidence, severity, and violation state. Do NOT use this cube for broad asset inventory fields (tags, reconciliation, interface details, provider raw JSON).

cubes.name: AssetInsightOnly
cubes.title: Asset Insight Only
cubes.description: Insight-only cube combining active insight rows with minimal asset status context. Grain is one row per active insight per asset, so a single asset can produce multiple rows when it has multiple active findings. Each row exposes the per-insight fields needed for security analysis, including classification, indicator, rule ID, state, confidence, severity, sub-classification, and sync timestamps, plus managed status for basic asset scoping. Use this cube when the question is about insight behaviour itself rather than broader asset inventory, for example "show active insights by severity", "count registration findings by confidence", or "list assets with a specific indicator rule". Choose this cube or AssetDetailsV1 over AssetDetailsAggV1 whenever the query groups by, breaks down by, or counts WITHIN any insight dimension - classification, sub-classification, indicator, indicator rule, confidence, severity, or state - because in both each insight is its own row and these are groupable scalar dimensions; in AssetDetailsAggV1 those same fields are per-asset arrays and cannot be grouped correctly. Use THIS cube when the breakdown is purely by insight dimensions with little or no asset attributes (e.g. "zombie assets by sub-classification", "breakdown of insights by severity"); use AssetDetailsV1 when the same query also groups by or returns asset attributes such as provider, OS, region, or vendor (e.g. "violated insights by provider and severity"). For asset inventory with rolled-up insight arrays - one row per asset, insight fields used only for filtering - use AssetDetailsAggV1. Time dimension: default to updated_at (insight sync time) scoped to the last 7 days from now (to the minute); if the user specifies a time range - for example "in the last 3 hours", "over the past 2 days", or "not in the last 3 days" - apply those constraints instead, as user-specified time always takes priority over the default.

cubes.name: AssetLocations
cubes.title: Asset Locations
cubes.description: Reference lookup cube mapping cloud provider region codes to human-readable location names and labels. One row per provider-region combination. Use for questions about available regions, region display labels, or provider listings. Supports filtering by provider, region code, and geographic location. Joined by other cubes to resolve region codes into display-friendly names. No measures - pure dimension table.

cubes.name: AssetProviderData
cubes.title: Asset Provider Data
cubes.description: Provider-data comparison cube combining raw provider-specific rows with a synthetic common row derived from aggregated asset data for each asset. Grain is one row per asset-provider-source record, plus one additional common row per asset that represents the merged asset view. Each row exposes provider-reported attributes such as provider identity, source table, raw JSON payload, sync time, name, asset type, OS and version, vendor, model, serial number, IP or MAC addresses, location, tags, and provider-specific first or last seen timestamps. The asset type (display_type) is populated only on the common row from the merged asset view; provider rows return an empty string when the provider does not supply a mapped asset type. Use this cube when a query needs provider-level differences or raw provider payloads, for example "compare device names across providers", "show raw provider JSON for this asset", "find which provider last saw an asset", "show asset type in provider comparison", or "review OS and serial mismatches between common and provider rows". Prefer this cube over broader asset cube when the question is specifically about per-provider provenance, disagreement, or raw source data.

cubes.name: AssetProviderDataAttrIndex
cubes.title: Asset Provider Data Attr Index
cubes.description: Flattened attribute search index over provider raw JSON. Grain is one row per distinct (account, provider, source_table, json_path, value) tuple - deduplicated, so a value shared by many assets collapses to a single row (asset identity is intentionally not part of the grain). Each row exposes the JSON path, its original ClickHouse datatype, and the value cast to String. Use this cube to power attribute search and value autocomplete, for example "list the distinct json paths a provider reports", "suggest values for json_path 'Architecture'", or "find paths whose name contains 'launch'". Backed by ngrams(3) full-text indexes on provider, source_table and json_path, so substring search on those columns is granule-accelerated. The columns form a cascading drill-down hierarchy - provider -> source_table -> json_path -> value - so narrow filters left-to-right (pick a provider, then a source_table, then a json_path) before suggesting values. For per-asset raw payloads or provider provenance use AssetProviderData instead; this cube is a distinct-attribute catalog, not a per-asset table.

cubes.name: AssetSource
cubes.title: Asset Sources
cubes.description: Lookup table of all discovery sources and providers in the asset platform. One row per unique source. Use for questions like 'what sources exist', 'list all providers', or 'show available discovery sources'. Supports filtering and grouping by source name or display label. Joined by asset cubes to resolve source identifiers to user-friendly labels.

cubes.name: AssetSubClassifications
cubes.title: Asset Sub Classifications
cubes.description: Lookup table mapping insight sub-classification codes to display labels, with one row per sub-classification. Sub-classifications use a "parent/child" path hierarchy across three types - zombie (e.g., "zombie/stale_device" -> "Stale Device"), compliance (e.g., "compliance/missing_patch" -> "Missing Patch"), and ghost (e.g., "ghost/discovery_gap" -> "Discovery Gap"). Use for questions about available sub-classifications, populating filter dropdowns, or resolving codes to friendly names. Supports filtering by zombie, compliance, and ghost insight types via segments. Joined by other asset cubes for sub-classification lookups - contains no measures. Example queries: "what sub-classifications exist", "list all zombie sub-types", "show compliance insight categories".

cubes.name: AssetSuperCategories
cubes.title: Asset Super Categories
cubes.description: Static lookup table enumerating top-level asset categories (Devices, Network, Services, Unverified). One row per category. Each represents a high-level grouping: "Devices" covers servers, workstations, laptops, IP phones, media devices, and power devices; "Network" covers routers, switches, firewalls, gateways, load balancers, subnets, and wireless controllers; "Services" covers DNS servers, storage, cloud services, and SaaS resources; "Unverified" covers ghost assets detected by one source but not confirmed by another. Use for questions like "what categories exist" or "list top-level asset groupings". Supports populating category filter dropdowns and validating category values. Example queries: "what categories exist", "list top-level asset groupings", "how many network devices do I have", "show all unverified assets".

cubes.name: AssetTypeLabels
cubes.title: Types
cubes.description: Dimension-only lookup cube mapping raw cloud resource type identifiers to human-readable display names, one row per resource type. Use for questions about what asset resource types exist, listing resource types, populating resource type filter dropdowns, or resolving resource codes to friendly names. Supports filtering by resource type code or display name. Use when asking "what asset resource types exist", "list resource types", or "show available resource types".

cubes.name: Asset_Insight_DeviceInterface_Agg_Expanded
cubes.title: Asset Insight - Device Interface (Aggregated, Expanded)
cubes.description: Join cube combining normalised asset attributes with network interface data. Each row represents one asset and exposes: (1) common asset fields -- name, OS, vendor, model, IP/MAC addresses, categories, location, managed status, first/last seen, tags, and source table; (2) aggregated security insights -- insight types, indicator IDs, confidence levels, severities, states, sub-classifications, and pre-computed composite keys like insight_types_confidence_levels; and (3) network interface attributes -- interface details like VRF names, IP addresses, MAC addresses, etc. Use this cube when a query needs BOTH common asset attributes AND network interface attributes -- for example "show me assets with specific interface configurations", "list devices with their network interfaces", or "filter assets by interface properties". Do NOT use this cube for insight-only or asset-only queries where interface data is not needed; prefer AssetDetails_ch_agg for those cases.

cubes.name: Asset_Insight_DeviceInterface_Expanded
cubes.title: Asset Insight - Device Interface (Expanded)
cubes.description: Join cube combining normalised asset attributes and network interface attributes. This non-aggregated version keeps insight rows at detailed grain, so one asset can produce multiple rows when multiple indicators/rules exist. Use this cube when a query needs BOTH asset/insight context AND interface-level fields such as interface name, VLANs, VRF, trunk status, link aggregation, switch/wireless info, or DHCP lease details. Example queries: "show active insights on assets connected to trunk interfaces", "list assets with failed registration insights and interface oper status down", or "find devices with specific VRF names and their insight indicators". Do NOT use this cube for provider raw attributes; use Asset_Insight_DeviceInterface_ProviderData_Expanded or Asset_Insight_ProviderData_Expanded when provider-specific columns are required.

cubes.name: Asset_Insight_DeviceInterface_ProviderData_Agg_Expanded
cubes.title: Asset Insight - Device Interface + Provider Data (Aggregated, Expanded)
cubes.description: Join cube combining normalised asset attributes with network interface data and raw provider discovery data. Each row represents one asset and exposes: (1) common asset fields -- name, OS, vendor, model, IP/MAC addresses, categories, location, managed status, first/last seen, tags, and source table; (2) aggregated security insights -- insight types, indicator IDs, confidence levels, severities, states, sub-classifications, and pre-computed composite keys like insight_types_confidence_levels; (3) network interface attributes -- interface details like VRF names, IP addresses, MAC addresses, etc.; and (4) raw provider attributes -- per-provider name, categories, OS, vendor, model, serial number, IPs, MACs, location, last seen, tags, pd_standardized_json_attributes, and the full pd_raw_json blob. Use this cube when a query needs BOTH common asset attributes AND BOTH network interface AND provider-specific attributes -- for example "show me AWS EC2 instances with their network interfaces and VPC configurations", "list devices with interface and provider data", or "filter assets by both interface properties and provider attributes". Do NOT use this cube for queries where either interface or provider data is not needed; prefer simpler cube like AssetDetails_ch_agg for those cases.

cubes.name: Asset_Insight_DeviceInterface_ProviderData_Expanded
cubes.title: Asset Insight - Device Interface + Provider Data (Expanded)
cubes.description: Join cube combining normalised asset attributes, network interface attributes, and provider-specific raw attributes. This non-aggregated version keeps detailed insight rows, so one asset can produce multiple rows across indicators/rules and joined provider/interface records. Use this cube when a query needs the broadest field coverage across asset + insight + interface + provider domains in one result set. Example queries: "show unacknowledged high-severity insights for assets where interface is trunk and provider model matches X", "find assets with insight state active, provider tags containing Y, and interface VLAN Z", or "compare provider OS/version with interface telemetry for impacted assets". Do NOT use this cube for simple asset-only or insight-only analysis; prefer AssetDetails_ch_agg for better simplicity and performance.

cubes.name: Asset_Insight_DeviceInterface_ProviderData_UserData_Agg_Expanded
cubes.title: Asset Insight - Device Interface + Provider Data + User Data (Aggregated, Expanded)
cubes.description: Join cube combining normalised asset attributes with network interface data, raw provider discovery data, and per-user identity data. Each row represents one asset and exposes: (1) common asset fields -- name, OS, vendor, model, IP/MAC addresses, categories, location, managed status, first/last seen, tags, and source table; (2) aggregated security insights -- insight types, indicator IDs, confidence levels, severities, states, sub-classifications, and pre-computed composite keys like insight_types_confidence_levels; (3) network interface attributes -- interface details like VRF names, IP addresses, MAC addresses, etc.; (4) raw provider attributes -- per-provider name, categories, OS, vendor, model, serial number, IPs, MACs, location, last seen, tags, pd_standardized_json_attributes, and the full pd_raw_json blob; and (5) user identity fields -- first/last name, login ID, email, provider, and per-action provider map for the most recent user who logged on in the last 7 days. Use this cube when a query needs asset + interface + provider + user domains together -- for example "show assets with VPC interface and provider data where a specific user recently logged on". Do NOT use this cube for queries where user, interface, or provider data is not needed; prefer simpler cubes for those cases.

cubes.name: Asset_Insight_DeviceInterface_ProviderData_UserData_Expanded
cubes.title: Asset Insight - Device Interface + Provider Data + User Data (Expanded)
cubes.description: Join cube combining normalised asset attributes, network interface attributes, provider-specific raw attributes, and per-user identity data. Grain is one row per asset-insight combination. Use this cube when a query needs the broadest field coverage across asset + insight + interface + provider + user domains in one result set. Example queries: "show high-severity insights for assets where interface is trunk and logged-on user matches X", "find assets with active insight, provider tags containing Y, and interface VLAN Z with recent user logon". Do NOT use this cube for simple asset-only or insight-only analysis; prefer AssetDetails_ch_agg for better simplicity and performance.

cubes.name: Asset_Insight_DeviceInterface_UserData_Agg_Expanded
cubes.title: Asset Insight - Device Interface + User Data (Aggregated, Expanded)
cubes.description: Join cube combining normalised asset attributes with network interface data. cubes.name: Asset_Insight_ProviderData_Agg_Expanded
cubes.title: Asset Insight - Provider Data (Aggregated, Expanded)
cubes.description: Join cube combining normalised asset attributes with raw provider discovery data. Each row represents one asset and exposes: (1) common asset fields -- name, OS, vendor, model, IP/MAC addresses, categories, location, managed status, first/last seen, tags, and source table; (2) aggregated security insights -- insight types, indicator IDs, confidence levels, severities, states, sub-classifications, and pre-computed composite keys like insight_types_confidence_levels; and (3) raw provider attributes -- per-provider name, categories, OS, vendor, model, serial number, IPs, MACs, location, last seen, tags, pd_standardized_json_attributes, and the full pd_raw_json blob. Use this cube when a query needs BOTH common asset attributes (shared across all providers) AND provider-specific attributes that are only available from a particular source -- for example "show me all Jamf Pro assets where disk encryption is enabled", "list AWS EC2 instances with their instance type and IAM role from the provider", or "show AWS EC2 instances with their VPC ID and security groups". Do NOT use this cube for insight-only or asset-only queries where provider raw data is not needed; prefer AssetDetails_ch_agg for those cases.

cubes.name: Asset_Insight_ProviderData_Expanded
cubes.title: Asset Insight - Provider Data (Expanded)
cubes.description: Join cube combining normalised asset attributes and provider-specific raw attributes. This non-aggregated version preserves detailed insight rows and provider-level columns such as pd_provider, pd_source_table, pd_ip_addresses, pd_mac_addresses, pd_tags, pd_standardized_json_attributes, and pd_raw_json. Use this cube when a query needs BOTH common asset/insight fields AND provider payload context, for example "show active compliance insights with provider-reported model and serial", "find assets by provider tag values and insight indicator", or "inspect provider JSON for assets with critical findings". Do NOT use this cube for interface-focused analysis; use Asset_Insight_DeviceInterface_Expanded or Asset_Insight_DeviceInterface_ProviderData_Expanded when interface fields are required.

For interface- or provider-specific raw fields, use the corresponding *_agg_expanded cubes.

cubes.name: Asset_Insight_UserData_Expanded
cubes.title: Asset Insight - User Data (Expanded)
cubes.description: Primary detailed asset-and-insight cube combining normalised asset attributes, active insight rows, and 7-day user logon counts. Grain is one row per asset-insight combination, so a single asset can produce multiple rows when it has multiple active insights. For rolled-up insight arrays with one row per asset prefer AssetDetails_ch_agg.

cubes.name: DeviceInterface
cubes.title: Device Interface
cubes.description: Network-interface cube enriched with asset context for the first attached device. Grain is one row per latest interface record for a device and interface name. Each row exposes interface-level details such as classification, description, sync time, IP and MAC assignments, admin or oper state, speed, VLANs, trunk and aggregation status, VRF metadata, switch or wireless connectivity details, DHCP lease information, IP-space mappings, and attached-device tuples, plus resolved fields for the connected asset such as name, vendor, model, OS, provider, region, status, and taxonomy category. Use this cube when the question is about interface topology or connectivity with asset context, for example "which asset is connected to this port", "show interfaces with attached device details", "find trunk ports connected to inactive assets", or "review switch or wireless connectivity alongside the attached asset identity". Prefer this cube over broader asset cubes when interface-specific state or attached-device relationships are the primary focus.

cubes.name: NetworkInsightsAddressBlock
cubes.title: Network Insights Address Block
cubes.description: IP address block inventory. One row per address block resource PER IP SPACE, showing only the latest state of each IPv4 or IPv6 block. The cube reads events generated since the start of the previous day, so it is a current-state snapshot and cannot show how any value changed over time. Blocks whose latest event is a deletion are excluded, so a deleted block is absent from this cube rather than present with a deletion marker. Address blocks are parent containers for subnets; for subnet-level data use NetworkInsightsSubnet. Use for block counts, per-block IP utilisation, and provider or IP space breakdowns.

meta.ai_context: Stored values are lower-case codes, not display names: protocol is 'ip4' or 'ip6' (never 'IPv4'/'IPv6'), and source is 'On-Prem' or 'Cloud' (never 'On-Premise'). Filter on the stored code, because a filter on a display name matches no rows and returns a count of 0 with HTTP 200 rather than an error. usage is a joined array rather than a single value, so a block can carry several indicators at once as one string such as 'DISCOVERED, IPAM'; filter it with the contains operator, since equals 'IPAM' silently omits every block that also carries another indicator.

cubes.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpClassification
cubes.title: Network Insights Dhcp Classification
cubes.description: DHCP classification events: IP addresses that the DHCP anomaly classifier has already flagged, as stale reservations, stale fixed addresses, rogue assignments or rapid requests. One row per address resource and classification type, showing the latest state. It holds only the most recent 24 hours of classifier evaluations and carries no history, so it cannot answer a question about change over time. Every row here is an address that is already flagged, so a count from this cube is a count of flagged addresses and never a total: for how many fixed addresses, reservations or leases exist, use the IPAM and DHCP REST APIs instead. For DHCP range utilization, use NetworkInsightsDhcpUtilization instead.

cubes.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpUtilization
cubes.title: Network Insights Dhcp Utilization
cubes.description: Per-range DHCP address utilization for the account: one row per DHCP range, carrying its total, used, free, static, dynamic and abandoned address counts, its utilization percentage and utilization tier, plus the range's name, start and end addresses, IP space, parent subnet, DHCP server or HA group, provider, access view, tags and comment. This is a CURRENT SNAPSHOT with no history: the underlying query keeps only the newest row per range from a 24-48 hour window, so utilization trends over time cannot be produced here even though the source table retains 13 months. Ranges deleted upstream are absent entirely. COVERAGE IS NOT GUARANTEED TO BE COMPLETE: IPv6 DHCP ranges have been observed present in the IPAM range data and absent from this cube, so a query here returning no IPv6 ranges does not establish that none are configured. Cross-check IPv6 questions against the IPAM range data. Individual lease records and lease start, expiry or renewal times are not here. Per-address DHCP anomalies are in NetworkInsightsDhcpClassification; subnet and address-block level utilization are in NetworkInsightsSubnetUtilization and NetworkInsightsAddressBlock.

cubes.name: NetworkInsightsDnsHostLookup
cubes.title: Network Insights Dns Host Lookup
cubes.description: One row per DNS host observed answering DNS queries within the retained window, derived from DNS query logs rather than from configuration. Retains roughly one day, so it holds no history and cannot show a trend; a requested range wider than a day returns the same rows rather than an error. A configured DNS server that served no query in the window does not appear at all, so a row count here is not a count of DNS servers: on a probed account this cube held 39 hosts while the DNS host configuration API held 61, the difference being external DNS providers, idle or erroring appliances, and grid members whose logs do not reach this pipeline. Has no measures: count hosts by reading rows. Carries no IP address, site, location, client identity or query-volume field.

meta.ai_context: DDI/Network Insights domain. Use it to resolve a DNS host identifier to a name, and to find when a host was last seen answering DNS queries. For a count or inventory of configured DNS servers, use the DNS host configuration API or the Infrastructure services inventory instead, because this cube only sees hosts that carried traffic. For DNS failures broken down by server, use NetworkInsightsDnsRawLogs, which already exposes the server name directly and needs no lookup from here. For a host's IP address, site or location, use the Infrastructure host inventory. For current query rate, use host service metrics. Absence of a host from this cube is not evidence that the host is idle or misconfigured, only that no DNS query from it reached this pipeline in the window.

cubes.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRawLogs
cubes.title: Network Insights Dns Raw Logs
cubes.description: Failed DNS transactions only, one row per failed event. Retains roughly three days. Successful lookups are not stored here, so this cube can tell you what is failing and where, but never total query volume, a success count, or a failure rate.

meta.ai_context: SCOPE: only DNS transactions that returned a non-zero response code are stored; the ingest view filters out every successful lookup. A count here is a count of failures, never of queries, and a filter for a successful response code returns an empty result rather than an error. WINDOW: roughly three days. A 7-day or 30-day request returns the same three days with no warning, and a window older than that returns no rows rather than an error, so an empty result means the data has expired, not that nothing failed. A requested span wider than 66 days is rejected, and every query must carry an explicit time range. NO CLIENT IDENTITY: no client IP, MAC, hostname or site; the server fields identify the DNS server that answered, not the device that asked. FIELD NAMES: server_name and server_id, view_name and view_id, zone_name and zone_id, qname, qtype, rcode, classification. There is no 'server', 'dns_view', 'response_code' or 'hour_of_day' field; for an hourly shape use a time dimension with hour granularity. DDI/Network Insights domain — DNS service health, not security. Use it for DNS resolution failures, response-code and error-pattern analysis, and query-type breakdowns per server, zone or view. Despite the name, 'Network Insights' is unrelated to Threat Defense insights: this cube holds no security actions, threat indicators, severities or enforcement outcomes. For any question about security events, blocked versus unblocked DNS activity, threat feeds, threat actors, or insights, use SecurityActionSummaryView, SecurityActionIndicators or SecurityActionAssets — or PortunusRawRpzLogs_ch_s for raw RPZ enforcement events.

cubes.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecords
cubes.title: Network Insights Dns Records
cubes.description: DNS record insight violation events showing which DNS records currently violate asset insight indicators. One row per violated indicator rule per DNS record, with severity, confidence, and acknowledgment status. Use for questions about DNS hygiene issues, stale records, violation counts by zone, provider, record type, or severity. For one row per unique DNS record with aggregated indicator lists, use NetworkInsightsDnsRecordsRolledByIndicatorId instead. Supports filtering by indicator, severity, zone, provider, record type, and acknowledgment status.

cubes.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecordsRolledByIndicatorId
cubes.title: Network Insights Dns Records Rolled by Indicator ID
cubes.description: DNS record hygiene findings rolled up to ONE ROW PER DNS RECORD, carrying the complete list of indicators that record violates. Use this for questions about which DNS records have problems, for listing records together with everything wrong with each one, and for counting how many RECORDS are affected. For a total number of individual findings, where a record with three problems counts as three, use NetworkInsightsDnsRecords, which keeps one row per finding. The category of each finding has readable values such as Stale, Dangling and Untrusted; group by the indicator list to see which are present rather than guessing a value. Contains only records that violate an indicator, so it cannot list compliant records and an empty result does not mean the estate is healthy; for the full DNS record inventory use the DNS record REST collection instead. Holds only the most recent evaluation of each record over a short trailing window, so it is a current-state snapshot rather than a history and cannot support a trend.

cubes.name: NetworkInsightsDnsViewLookup
cubes.title: Network Insights Dns View Lookup
cubes.description: Maps a DNS view's opaque identifier to its administrator-assigned name, one row per view. NOT AN INVENTORY OF CONFIGURED VIEWS: rows appear only for views observed carrying DNS traffic in roughly the last day, so this list can be much shorter than the account's configured views and can also contain the literal '_default', which is not a configured view object. For what is configured, and for anything about how a view is set up - the zones it serves, its client-match criteria, its IP spaces - use the DnsConfig service /dns/view and /dns/auth_zone endpoints; none of that is in this cube. This cube has NO MEASURES of any kind: pass an empty measures list and read the answer from the dimensions, and count DNS views by counting rows. It is a CURRENT SNAPSHOT, not a history: the SQL keeps one row per view, so grouping by day yields a single bucket and no trend over time can be produced here. It carries no query counts, no response codes and no client detail; for total DNS query volume per view use NstarDnsActivity (dimension dns_view, measure total_query_count) and for failed-query volume per view use NetworkInsightsDnsRawLogs. Unlike NetworkInsightsDnsRawLogs, whose source is restricted to failed responses, this cube is built from all DNS transactions, so its coverage caveats do not apply here.

cubes.name: NetworkInsightsDnsZoneLookup
cubes.title: Network Insights Dns Zone Lookup
cubes.description: Maps a DNS zone's opaque identifier to its fully qualified domain name, one row per zone. NOT AN INVENTORY OF CONFIGURED ZONES: rows appear only for zones named in an observed DNS query within roughly the last day, so this list can be a small fraction of the account's configured zones and a row count here is NOT the account's zone count. For how many DNS zones exist, and for anything about how a zone is set up, use the DnsConfig service /dns/auth_zone and /dns/forward_zone endpoints, or TokenUtilManagementObjectsDaily with object_sub_type 'DNS Zones' for a per-day configured count. This cube also BLENDS zone kinds it cannot distinguish: an identifier here can belong to an authoritative zone or to a forward zone, with no dimension saying which, and reverse in-addr.arpa zones sit in the same list as forward ones. This cube has NO MEASURES of any kind: pass an empty measures list and read the answer from the dimensions, counting rows rather than looking for a count measure. It is a CURRENT SNAPSHOT, not a history: the SQL keeps only the newest record per zone, so grouping by day cannot yield a trend and no zone-count history can be produced here. It carries no query counts, no response codes, no record inventory and no client detail. For DNS failures broken down by zone use NetworkInsightsDnsRawLogs, which counts FAILED responses only; total DNS query volume per zone is not available through this interface. For per-zone record data use NetworkInsightsDnsRecords. For DNS host name lookups use NetworkInsightsDnsHostLookup and for DNS view name lookups use NetworkInsightsDnsViewLookup.

cubes.name: NetworkInsightsOverlappingBlocksBase
cubes.title: Network Insights Overlapping Blocks Base
cubes.description: Per-object rows for cross-IP-space IP address overlap detection: one row per overlapping object per shared address CIDR per IP space. In each row the object being described is the one whose CIDR is overlap_address; the `address` field is the shared range that object sits inside, and it is the key the overlap group is formed on. Holds only about the last day of detections and no history at all, so no trend or change-over-time question can be answered here, and queries should carry no date range: any window narrower than the cube's own span silently returns only part of the current state. Detection is change-driven rather than an inventory sweep: an object is re-evaluated only when its address changes or when it is re-synced, so this cube can hold far fewer overlaps than exist in the IP address management data. Use NetworkInsightsOverlappingBlocksList to count the blocks and subnets involved, and NetworkInsightsOverlappingBlocksRolled for a per-shared-range summary; this cube's only measure counts shared ranges, not objects.

cubes.name: NetworkInsightsOverlappingBlocksList
cubes.title: Network Insights Overlapping Blocks List
cubes.description: Deduplicated inventory of the address blocks and subnets involved in cross-IP-space IP overlaps, one row per object per IP space. This is the cube that answers 'how many of my blocks and subnets are overlapping' and 'list the overlapping objects': its count and overlap_count measures are the only ones in this family that count objects. In each row the object being described is the one whose CIDR is overlap_address; the `address` field is the shared range that object sits inside. Holds only about the last day of detections and no history, so no trend question can be answered here, and queries should carry no date range: any window narrower than the cube's own span silently returns only part of the current count. Detection is change-driven rather than an inventory sweep, so this cube can hold far fewer overlaps than exist in the IP address management data. Utilisation, DHCP settings, tags, comments and access views are not carried here; those live on the IPAM subnet and address block collections. For a per-shared-range summary use NetworkInsightsOverlappingBlocksRolled.

meta.ai_context: An overlap needs at least two surviving objects on the same range. Rows here are detections, not live conflicts: a range can still appear here after its counterparts were deleted from IPAM, in which case it is not currently overlapping anything and must not be listed as a live overlap. Do not test for that by grouping this cube on address: the deduplication here drops address from its key, so which shared range an object keeps is arbitrary. Take the surviving-claimant count from NetworkInsightsOverlappingBlocksRolled.overlap_count, unfiltered, and treat a range whose count is 1 as a stale detection rather than an overlap.

cubes.name: NetworkInsightsOverlappingBlocksRolled
cubes.title: Network Insights Overlapping Blocks Rolled
cubes.description: Cross-IP-space IP overlap detection rolled up to one row per shared address range per tenant, with the number of objects claiming that range and the lists of IP spaces, discovery sources and platforms involved. It carries no per-object detail and no time dimension: there are no object names, types, providers or identifiers here, and no way to bound or bucket a query in time, so the answer is always the current snapshot covering roughly the last day of detections. For per-object detail, or for any question that needs a time range, use NetworkInsightsOverlappingBlocksList. Detection is change-driven rather than an inventory sweep, so this cube can hold far fewer overlaps than exist in the IP address management data.

meta.ai_context: Rows here are detections, not live conflicts. Always project overlap_count alongside address. In an unfiltered query, overlap_count = 1 means no counterpart survives: the other claimants were dropped after the overlap group was formed (in every case root-caused so far, because the object had been deleted from IPAM), and on some tenants most rows are of this kind. Do not present such a row as a live overlapping network, and do not read its one-element space_names_str as a namespace overlapping itself: exclude those rows and say how many you excluded, or list them separately as stale detections whose counterpart no longer exists. Never combine that test with a providers_str or sources_str filter. Those two are pushed into the pre-aggregation and rewrite overlap_count to the filtered subset, so a live overlap reports 1 there and the test silently deletes it. To scope an answer to one provider or source, query this cube unfiltered and narrow the rows afterwards with query_stored_data.

cubes.name: NetworkInsightsSubnet
cubes.title: Network Insights Subnet
cubes.description: IP subnets (IPv4 and IPv6) within IP spaces. One row per subnet PER IP SPACE, holding only the latest state, so the same CIDR can legitimately appear many times. Use for subnet inventory, per-subnet IP utilization, DHCP status, provider breakdown and federated realm membership. Deleted subnets are absent. For utilization trends over time use NetworkInsightsSubnetUtilization; for ranges that overlap across IP spaces use the NetworkInsightsOverlappingBlocks cubes.

meta.ai_context: Every row is the CURRENT state of a subnet, captured in a single refresh within roughly the last day; there is no ingest-time or snapshot-time field to query and no older revision to compare against. Grain is one row per subnet per IP space; `ref_id_resource_id` is the row identity and `address` is not unique. Because the cube holds one snapshot rather than history, no trend, no growth rate and no as-at-a-past-date answer can come from it: for utilization over time use NetworkInsightsSubnetUtilization, and for a subnet's own lifecycle dates use `created_at` and `updated_at`, which do span years. `count` is the only measure: every utilization field is a per-subnet dimension, so totals and averages over them are not available here and placing one in `measures` fails. Combined IPv4+IPv6 utilization percentages are not comparable across protocols, because an IPv6 prefix contributes its whole address space to the denominator. Several string fields are joined multi-value strings whose element order is not stable, so match them with `contains` rather than `equals` and treat a group-by on them as approximate. A time range is only honoured on `created_at` and `updated_at`, and is limited to 400 days.

cubes.name: NetworkInsightsSubnetUtilization
cubes.title: Network Insights Subnet Utilization
cubes.description: Account-wide IPv4/IPv6 address utilisation as a daily time series, one aggregate row per day, covering today plus the previous seven calendar days. This is the only source of a multi-day utilisation trend. It carries NO subnet identity, no IP space and no protocol dimension, so it cannot show, filter to, group by or rank an individual subnet, space or protocol; for any of those, and for current per-subnet state or a subnet count, use NetworkInsightsSubnet or the IPAM subnet API. A date range wider than the window is accepted without error and silently returns only the days that exist, so a longer trend cannot be produced here. The single utilisation percentage measure needs a filter to be meaningful: read its description before using it.

meta.ai_context: Grain: one aggregate row per day, today plus the previous seven calendar days. There is no count measure and no subnet, IP space or protocol dimension, so subnet counts, per-subnet figures, rankings and breakdowns are not answerable here and belong to NetworkInsightsSubnet or the IPAM subnet API. IMPORTANT: utilization_percentage sums IPv6 address-space sizes together with IPv4 address counts, so without the filter utilization_v6_total == 0 it returns a figure many orders of magnitude below the real one. Align any date range to whole days: a partial first day covers only part of the fleet and reads far higher than the real figure. Aggregate it at a day granularity; grouping it by the raw snapshot timestamp returns a plausible-looking percentage that belongs to no identifiable subnet. Do not attempt to rebuild a total by pulling the per-subnet counters and summing them: with no subnet identity the rows deduplicate and the sum comes out short. Only one measure exists, utilization_percentage, and it requires an explicit date range.

cubes.name: NetworkNstarDhcpLeaseActivity
cubes.title: Nstar DHCP Lease Activity (ClickHouse)
cubes.description: DHCP lease activity data including lease assignments, renewals, and terminations. Captures per-lease details such as leased IP address, MAC address, client hostname, DHCP fingerprint, lease operation type, lease lifecycle timestamps (start/end), protocol (IPv4/IPv6), IP space, host and subnet context, and lease state — for comprehensive DHCP monitoring and reporting.

meta.ai_context: ⚠️ NIOS DHCP lease logs are not queryable via this cube. This is a known limitation. Instead of telling the user that there are no lease records for a NIOS DHCP server, you should make clear that this is a known limitation.

cubes.name: NetworkNstarDnsActivity
cubes.title: Nstar DNS Activity (ClickHouse)
cubes.description: DNS activity data including client queries, device information, and DHCP fingerprints. Captures per-query details such as query name, type, response code, client/device identifiers (IP, MAC, hostname), DNS view context, site and IP-space associations, user/device group memberships, and nanosecond-precision timestamps for comprehensive DNS monitoring and reporting.

cubes.name: PortunusRawRpzLogs_ch_s
cubes.title: Portunus Raw Rpz Logs Ch S
cubes.description: Per-event RPZ (Response Policy Zone) enforcement records from td_raw_rpz_dist, one row per RPZ action. Use for questions about security policy enforcement: blocked domains, threat indicators, policy actions, threat classifications, feed attribution, and actor analysis. Supports filtering by domain (qname/domain/sld), client IP (qip), response IP (rip), policy (policy_name/policy_id/policy_action), threat metadata (severity/tclass/tproperty/tfamily/confidence), feed (feed_name/feed_type/category), actor (actor_id/actor_name), device (device_name/mac_address), user, geographic location, and time. For DNS-only logs, use PortunusDnsLogs_ch_s.

meta.ai_context: Raw per-event RPZ log, NOT the Threat Defense insight model. Use it only when the question is genuinely about individual DNS/RPZ transactions — a specific domain's raw hits, per-client-IP query volume, or raw event counts over time with no reference to insights. If the question mentions insights or security actions in any form — counting them, listing them, their severity, status, policy, feed, threat actor, blocked versus unblocked outcome, or the assets and indicators belonging to them — use SecurityActionSummaryView, SecurityActionIndicators or SecurityActionAssets instead, even though this cube also carries domain, policy, feed, threat and actor fields. Those fields describe raw events here, not insights, and aggregating them will not reproduce insight-level answers.

cubes.name: SecurityActionAssets
cubes.title: Security Action Assets
cubes.description: Per-asset detail for security actions, one row per asset per security action. Terminology: "insight" is the user-facing alias for "security action" in the IQ Threat Defense UI — treat the two terms as synonyms. Each record describes a device including network identifiers (IP, MAC, hostname), threat indicators on the asset, associated users, event counts, verification status, risk flag, provider/region, ranking, and first/last detection timeline. Scope: rows created in the last 30 days where the parent security action has visible=true and evaluation_start_date within the last 30 days (matching SecurityActionSummaryView's scope). Use this cube to check all assets involved for a particular security action, or to see all risky assets across security actions — it's suggested to use it with securityActionDisplayId in the filter when scoping to a single security action. For security action-level summaries use SecurityActionSummaryView; for indicator-level drill-downs use SecurityActionIndicators.

meta.ai_context: IQ Threat Defense domain. Device detail inside insights/security actions: use it only when the unit of the answer is an individual asset — which devices are involved in a given insight, asset IP/MAC/hostname, per-asset risk flag, verification status, or asset ranking within an insight. Do NOT use it to count or compare insights themselves (it returns one row per asset per insight and will double-count); for questions like 'insights affecting more than N assets', 'how many insights', or breakdowns across insights use SecurityActionSummaryView. NOT a DDI/network or asset-inventory cube: distinct from AssetDetails_ch, Asset_Insight_* and all NetworkInsights* cubes, which are unrelated to Threat Defense insights.

cubes.name: SecurityActionIndicators
cubes.title: Security Action Indicators
cubes.description: Threat indicator detail for security actions, one row per indicator per security action. Terminology: "insight" is the user-facing alias for "security action" in the IQ Threat Defense UI — treat the two terms as synonyms. Each record describes an IOC (domain, IP, URL) including threat level, confidence rating, threat actor, event volume, affected verified/unverified assets, associated users, enforcement action status, and first/last detection timeline. Scope: rows created in the last 30 days where the parent security action has visible=true and evaluation_start_date within the last 30 days (matching SecurityActionSummaryView's scope). Use this cube to check all threat indicators involved for a particular security action, or to see all high-severity / high-confidence indicators across security actions — it's suggested to use it with securityActionDisplayId in the filter when scoping to a single security action. For security action-level summaries use SecurityActionSummaryView; for asset-level drill-downs use SecurityActionAssets.

meta.ai_context: IQ Threat Defense domain. Indicator-of-compromise detail inside insights/security actions: use it when the unit of the answer is the indicator (domain, IP, URL) — indicators shared across more than one insight, indicator threat level or confidence, threat actor per indicator, enforcement outcome per indicator, and blocked versus unblocked DNS event counts attributed to indicators. This is the correct cube for blocked/unblocked DNS event breakdowns within Threat Defense insights. NOT a DDI/network cube: it does not hold raw DNS query logs, DNS records, zones or views — do not confuse it with NetworkInsightsDnsRawLogs, NetworkInsightsDnsRecords or other NetworkInsights* cubes. For whole-insight counts use SecurityActionSummaryView; for device detail use SecurityActionAssets.

cubes.name: SecurityActionSummaryView
cubes.title: Security Action Summary View
cubes.description: Security action inventory — one row per visible security action (canonical leads and similar/non-canonical group members). Terminology: "insight" is the user-facing name for a security action in the IQ Threat Defense UI — treat "insight" and "security action" as synonyms. Scope: rows where visible=true and evaluation_start_date is within the last 30 days — expired security actions (evaluation window older than 30 days) are excluded entirely, so expiringInDays never returns -1 in this cube. ALWAYS filter isCanonical = true for the primary inventory and for questions like "how many insights" — otherwise similar members are mixed in and counts double. For similar insights linked to a lead, filter isCanonical = false AND groupId equals the canonical securityActionID. Key fields: name, description, severity (Low/Medium/High/Critical), currentStatus, impact counts, effort metrics, threat context, evaluation window, isCanonical, groupId, and derived expiringInDays. For per-security-action drill-downs use SecurityActionAssets / SecurityActionIndicators / SecurityActionRecommendations (those stay scoped to canonical parents).

meta.ai_context: IQ Threat Defense domain. This is the insight/security-action inventory: use it whenever the question counts, lists, groups, or compares whole insights rather than their contents — how many insights, insights by severity or status, resolved vs unresolved, reopened, expiring or expiry window, threat property or threat class breakdown across insights, threat feed attribution across insights, threat actor for a named insight, insights affecting more than N assets, insights involving a named user. Prefer this cube over SecurityActionAssets and SecurityActionIndicators whenever the unit of the answer is the insight itself; those two return one row per asset or per indicator and will double-count insights. NOT a DDI/network cube: unrelated to NetworkInsights* (DNS records, zones, views, subnets, address blocks, DHCP) and to raw DNS/RPZ logs. This cube also holds IQ automation time-savings data via measures totalTimeSaved, totalManualTime, and totalAgentTime.

cubes.name: ActionsV1
cubes.title: Actions
cubes.description: AI-driven recommended actions tracking alerts and insights across DNS and infrastructure services. One row per action. Use for questions about open alerts, action severity distribution, resolution status, affected servers, and action timelines. Supports filtering by type, severity, status, affected resource, and creation/resolution date.

meta.ai_context: Use action_count for totals. Filter on severity and status for triage views. action_id is the primary key. event_timestamp is when the triggering event occurred; created_on is when the action was created.

cubes.name: assetinsightindicators
cubes.title: Indicators
cubes.description: Lookup table of asset insight indicator types and display labels, one row per indicator. No measures - pure dimension table used for labeling and filtering insight indicators across dashboards and reports. Use for questions about available indicators, indicator keys, and human-readable labels. Supports filtering by indicator name or display label.

cubes.name: assetinsightsubclassifications
cubes.title: SubClassifications
cubes.description: Lookup table of asset insight sub-classification types, one row per sub-classification. No measures - pure dimension table used for labeling and segmenting asset insights. Use for questions about available sub-classifications, their display labels, and parent classification categories. Supports filtering by classification category (zombie, compliance, ghost) and sub-classification name.

cubes.name: assetinsighttypes
cubes.title: Classifications
cubes.description: Lookup table of asset insight classification types (also called insight types), one row per classification. No measures - pure dimension table used for labeling the top-level category of asset insights. Use for questions about available insight classifications and their display labels. Supports filtering by classification name or display label.

cubes.name: HostMetrics
cubes.title: Host Metrics
cubes.description:
Infrastructure health metrics for on-premises hosts running DNS, DHCP, and NTP services, with one row per metric data point per host.

IMPORTANT: These are internal metric identifiers for querying only.
When presenting results to users, describe what you found without
mentioning the specific metric names (e.g., say 'DNS queries per second'
instead of 'dns_qps_iq_5m').

Available Host Metrics:

DNS Query Metrics:
- dns_qps_iq_5m: DNS queries per second
- dns_nxrrset_count_iq_5m: Count of DNS queries returning no resource records
- dns_recursion_count_iq_5m: Count of recursive DNS queries
- dns_nxdomain_count_iq_5m: Count of DNS queries returning NXDOMAIN
- dns_servfail_count_iq_5m: Count of DNS queries returning SERVFAIL
- dns_referral_count_iq_5m: Count of DNS referral responses
- dns_timeout_rate_iq_5m: Count of DNS timeout responses
- ddns_ups_iq_5m: Dynamic DNS updates per second
- cache_hit_ratio_iq_5m: Cache hit ratio for DNS queries
- object_count_dns_iq_5m: DNS object count (number of records, zones, etc.)
- dns_refused_count_iq_5m: Count of DNS queries returning REFUSED
- total_query_count_iq_5m: Total number of DNS queries received

DNS Performance Metrics:
- dns_success_percent_iq_5m: Percentage of successful DNS queries
- dns_refused_percent_iq_5m: Percentage of DNS queries returning REFUSED
- dns_nxdomain_percent_iq_5m: Percentage of DNS queries returning NXDOMAIN
- dns_servfail_percent_iq_5m: Percentage of DNS queries returning SERVFAIL

DNS Latency Metrics:
- dns_latency_all_iq_5m: Overall DNS query latency
- dns_latency_auth_iq_5m: Authoritative DNS server response latency
- dns_latency_upstream_iq_5m: Upstream DNS server response latency

Host System Metrics:
- host_cpu_iq_5m: Host CPU utilization
- host_memory_iq_5m: Host memory utilization

Service Status Metrics:
- dns_status_iq_5m: DNS service health status
- anycast_status_iq_5m: Anycast service health status

DHCP Metrics:
- object_count_dhcp_iq_5m: DHCP object count (number of DHCP-related objects)
- dhcp_discover_iq_5m: Count of DHCPv4 DISCOVER packets received
- dhcp6_solicit_iq_5m: Count of DHCPv6 SOLICIT packets received
- dhcp_cumulative_assigned_addresses_iq_5m: Count of newly assigned DHCPv4 addresses
- dhcp6_cumulative_assigned_nas_iq_5m: Count of newly assigned DHCPv6 non-temporary addresses (NA)
- dhcp6_cumulative_assigned_pds_iq_5m: Count of newly assigned DHCPv6 prefix delegations (PD)
- dhcp_declined_addresses_iq_5m: Count of DHCPv4 declined addresses
- dhcp6_declined_addresses_iq_5m: Count of DHCPv6 declined addresses
- dhcp_demand_gap_iq_5m: Difference between DHCPv4 demand (DISCOVER) and assigned addresses
- dhcp6_demand_gap_iq_5m: Difference between DHCPv6 demand (SOLICIT) and assigned NAs/PDs
- dhcp_lease_reuses_iq_5m: Count of DHCPv4 lease reuses

cubes.name: HostServiceMetrics
cubes.title: Host Service Metrics
cubes.description:
Metrics data for hosts and services with managed/unmanaged filtering, including performance, status, and location information. Preferable to HostMetrics for user-facing tasks that require a display name

IMPORTANT: These are internal metric identifiers for querying only.
When presenting results to users, describe what you found without
mentioning the specific metric names (e.g., say 'DNS queries per second'
instead of 'dns_qps_iq_5m').

Available Host Metrics:

DNS Query Metrics:
- dns_qps_iq_5m: DNS queries per second
- dns_nxrrset_count_iq_5m: Count of DNS queries returning no resource records
- dns_recursion_count_iq_5m: Count of recursive DNS queries
- dns_nxdomain_count_iq_5m: Count of DNS queries returning NXDOMAIN
- dns_servfail_count_iq_5m: Count of DNS queries returning SERVFAIL
- dns_referral_count_iq_5m: Count of DNS referral responses
- dns_timeout_rate_iq_5m: Count of DNS timeout responses
- ddns_ups_iq_5m: Dynamic DNS updates per second
- cache_hit_ratio_iq_5m: Cache hit ratio for DNS queries
- object_count_dns_iq_5m: DNS object count (number of records, zones, etc.)
- dns_refused_count_iq_5m: Count of DNS queries returning REFUSED
- total_query_count_iq_5m: Total number of DNS queries received

DNS Performance Metrics:
- dns_success_percent_iq_5m: Percentage of successful DNS queries
- dns_refused_percent_iq_5m: Percentage of DNS queries returning REFUSED
- dns_nxdomain_percent_iq_5m: Percentage of DNS queries returning NXDOMAIN
- dns_servfail_percent_iq_5m: Percentage of DNS queries returning SERVFAIL

DNS Latency Metrics:
- dns_latency_all_iq_5m: Overall DNS query latency
- dns_latency_auth_iq_5m: Authoritative DNS server response latency
- dns_latency_upstream_iq_5m: Upstream DNS server response latency

Host System Metrics:
- host_cpu_iq_5m: Host CPU utilization
- host_memory_iq_5m: Host memory utilization

Service Status Metrics:
- dns_status_iq_5m: DNS service health status
- anycast_status_iq_5m: Anycast service health status

DHCP Metrics:
- object_count_dhcp_iq_5m: DHCP object count (number of DHCP-related objects)
- dhcp_discover_iq_5m: Count of DHCPv4 DISCOVER packets received
- dhcp6_solicit_iq_5m: Count of DHCPv6 SOLICIT packets received
- dhcp_cumulative_assigned_addresses_iq_5m: Count of newly assigned DHCPv4 addresses
- dhcp6_cumulative_assigned_nas_iq_5m: Count of newly assigned DHCPv6 non-temporary addresses (NA)
- dhcp6_cumulative_assigned_pds_iq_5m: Count of newly assigned DHCPv6 prefix delegations (PD)
- dhcp_declined_addresses_iq_5m: Count of DHCPv4 declined addresses
- dhcp6_declined_addresses_iq_5m: Count of DHCPv6 declined addresses
- dhcp_demand_gap_iq_5m: Difference between DHCPv4 demand (DISCOVER) and assigned addresses
- dhcp6_demand_gap_iq_5m: Difference between DHCPv6 demand (SOLICIT) and assigned NAs/PDs
- dhcp_lease_reuses_iq_5m: Count of DHCPv4 lease reuses

cubes.name: ip_history
cubes.title: IP History
cubes.description: IP-history cube that reconstructs contiguous assignment windows for currently active asset and IP pairs. Grain is one row per asset, IP address, and contiguous time period, where gaps of at least one day start a new history segment. Each row exposes the asset CQID, name, resource type, categories, deployment context, the assigned IP address, and the start and end timestamps for that assignment interval. Use this cube when the question is about IP ownership over time, for example "when did this asset have this IP", "which assets used a given IP", "show IP changes for an asset", or "review the timeline of active IP assignments". Prefer this cube over broader asset cubes when temporal IP assignment history is the primary focus.

cubes.name: MSPUtilizationDaily
cubes.title: Msp Utilization Daily
cubes.description: Daily security service usage metrics across managed tenant accounts for consumption tracking and billing.

cubes.name: TokenUtilManagement
cubes.title: Token Util Management
cubes.description: Token consumption for Universal DDI management objects, with one row per account per object type showing the latest available data. Use for questions about token usage by management object type, current token counts, and data freshness. Supports filtering by object type and account.

cubes.name: TokenUtilProtoSrvAAS
cubes.title: Token Util Proto Srv Aas
cubes.description: Hourly token utilization for protocol servers delivered as a service, at the grain of one row per account, instance type, and hour. Use for questions about token consumption volume, server instance counts, and usage trends over time. Supports filtering by instance type and time range. For daily or monthly trend analysis, use TokenUtilProtoSrvAASDaily or TokenUtilProtoSrvAASMonthly. For daily over-limit checks, use TokenUtilProtoSrvAASIsOver.

cubes.name: TokenUtilProtoSrvAASIsOver
cubes.title: Token Util Proto Srv Aas Is over
cubes.description: Daily threshold breach tracking for protocol servers delivered as a service. One row per protocol server instance per day. Use for questions about which as-a-service protocol servers are exceeding token utilization limits, over-limit counts, and threshold breach trends. Supports filtering by instance type, service connection, universal service, and time period.

cubes.name: TokenUtilProtoSrvSM
cubes.title: Token Util Proto Srv Sm
cubes.description: Tracks hourly license token utilization for self-managed (on-premises) protocol servers, with one row per account, instance type, and hour. Use for questions about token consumption, server instance counts, and utilization trends over time. Supports filtering by server size tier and time range. For daily per-host detail with over-utilization flags, use TokenUtilProtoSrvSMIsOver. For daily or monthly trend aggregations, use TokenUtilProtoSrvSMDaily or TokenUtilProtoSrvSMMonthly.

cubes.name: TokenUtilProtoSrvSMIsOver
cubes.title: Token Util Proto Srv Sm Is over
cubes.description: Daily per-host utilization for self-managed protocol servers, one row per server per day. Identifies servers exceeding capacity thresholds for QPS, LPS, and managed objects via the is_over flag. Use for questions about which servers are over-utilized, capacity breach counts, and per-host workload metrics. Supports filtering by instance type, host type, and host name. For aggregate token consumption without per-host detail, use TokenUtilProtoSrvSM or TokenUtilProtoSrvSMDaily instead.

cubes.name: TokenUtilReporting
cubes.title: Token Util Reporting
cubes.description: Daily token utilization reporting for license entitlements. One row per account per category per day. Use for questions about token consumption, utilization event counts, and usage trends over time. Supports filtering by category and time period. For each account, data reflects the latest non-extrapolated snapshot.

meta.ai_context: Infoblox has multiple types of tokens, of which 'reporting' is a specialized type. This cube represents the utilization of tokens of the type 'Reporting'. It is not a general-purpose cube for all tokens, but rather a specialized cube for 'reporting'-type tokens.

cubes.name: TokenUtilManagementDaily
cubes.title: Token Util Management Daily
cubes.description: Daily peak token consumption trends for Universal DDI management objects, with one row per account per object type per day. Use for questions about historical token usage patterns, daily consumption trends, and peak utilization over time. Supports filtering by object type, account, and date range.

cubes.name: TokenUtilManagementObjectsDaily
cubes.title: Token Util Management Objects Daily
cubes.description: Daily trend of management object counts and token consumption at peak utilization hour for Universal DDI license entitlements, with one row per day per object sub-type per deployment category. Use for questions about day-over-day changes in DDI resource counts (DNS zones, IP spaces, DHCP ranges, etc.) and their token usage. Unlike TokenUtilManagementObjects, which shows a latest snapshot, this cube provides historical daily trends. Supports filtering by object type, sub-type, and category.

cubes.name: TokenUtilProtoSrvAASDaily
cubes.title: Token Util Proto Srv Aas Daily
cubes.description: Tracks daily token utilization trends for protocol servers delivered as a service, with one row per account, instance type, and day based on peak-hour consumption. Use for questions about daily token usage patterns, consumption trends over time, and server instance counts. For hourly granularity, use TokenUtilProtoSrvAAS. For monthly trends, use TokenUtilProtoSrvAASMonthly. Supports filtering by instance type and date range.

cubes.name: TokenUtilProtoSrvSMDaily
cubes.title: Token Util Proto Srv Sm Daily
cubes.description: Daily token utilization trends for self-managed protocol servers (NIOS-X on-premises). One row per account per instance type per day, representing the peak-hour snapshot of token consumption. Use for questions about daily token usage trends, server counts by size tier, and day-over-day utilization comparisons. Supports filtering by instance type and date. For hourly granularity, use TokenUtilProtoSrvSM. For monthly trends, use TokenUtilProtoSrvSMMonthly.

cubes.name: TokenUtilReportingDaily
cubes.title: Token Util Reporting Daily
cubes.description: Provides daily historical trend data for token utilization across reporting service categories. One row per account, category, and day, representing the daily high-water-mark of token consumption. Use for questions about token usage trends over time, month-over-month comparisons, and daily consumption patterns. Unlike TokenUtilReporting which shows only the latest snapshot, this cube provides time-series history. Supports filtering by category and time period.
