full.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpClassification
full.title: Network Insights Dhcp Classification
full.description: DHCP classification events: IP addresses that the DHCP anomaly classifier has already flagged, as stale reservations, stale fixed addresses, rogue assignments or rapid requests. One row per address resource and classification type, showing the latest state. It holds only the most recent 24 hours of classifier evaluations and carries no history, so it cannot answer a question about change over time. Every row here is an address that is already flagged, so a count from this cube is a count of flagged addresses and never a total: for how many fixed addresses, reservations or leases exist, use the IPAM and DHCP REST APIs instead. For DHCP range utilization, use NetworkInsightsDhcpUtilization instead.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpClassification.account_id
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Classification Account ID
dimensions.description: Internal tenant account identifier, automatically filtered by the platform's security context to enforce data isolation. Use when grouping classification data by tenant account.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpClassification.id_application_name
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Classification ID Application Name
dimensions.description: The application identifier for the address resource that received the DHCP classification. Use when filtering classifications by originating application. Part of the address identity triple with id_resource_type and id_resource_id.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpClassification.id_resource_type
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Classification ID Resource Type
dimensions.description: The resource type of the address that received the DHCP classification. Use when filtering by address resource type. Part of the address identity triple with id_application_name and id_resource_id.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpClassification.id_resource_id
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Classification ID Resource ID
dimensions.description: Unique resource identifier of the IP address that received the DHCP classification. Primary key component for row-level uniqueness. Use when looking up classifications for a specific address. Part of the address identity triple with id_application_name and id_resource_type.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpClassification.address
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Classification Address
dimensions.description: The IP address that has a DHCP classification. Use when searching or filtering classifications by a specific IP address, or when displaying the affected address in results.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpClassification.subnet_id_application_name
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Classification Subnet ID Application Name
dimensions.description: The application identifier of the subnet containing the classified address. Use when filtering classifications by the subnet's originating application. Part of the subnet identity group with subnet_id_resource_type, subnet_id_resource_id, and subnet_address.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpClassification.subnet_id_resource_type
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Classification Subnet ID Resource Type
dimensions.description: The resource type of the subnet containing the classified address. Use when filtering by subnet resource type. Part of the subnet identity group with subnet_id_application_name, subnet_id_resource_id, and subnet_address.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpClassification.subnet_id_resource_id
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Classification Subnet ID Resource ID
dimensions.description: Unique resource identifier of the subnet containing the classified address. Use when looking up classifications for a specific subnet by ID. For the subnet's CIDR range, use subnet_address instead.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpClassification.subnet_address
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Classification Subnet Address
dimensions.description: The CIDR of the subnet containing the flagged address. This is a label, not an identity: two different subnets in different IP spaces can carry the same CIDR, and grouping by this field merges them. Group by subnet_id_resource_id when subnet identity matters.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpClassification.ip_space_id_application_name
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Classification Ip Space ID Application Name
dimensions.description: The application identifier for the IP space containing the classified address. Use when filtering by the IP space's originating application. Part of the IP space identity triple with ip_space_id_resource_type and ip_space_id_resource_id.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpClassification.ip_space_id_resource_type
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Classification Ip Space ID Resource Type
dimensions.description: The resource type of the IP space containing the classified address. Use when filtering by IP space resource type. Part of the IP space identity triple with ip_space_id_application_name and ip_space_id_resource_id.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpClassification.ip_space_id_resource_id
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Classification Ip Space ID Resource ID
dimensions.description: Unique resource identifier of the IP space containing the classified address. Use when querying classifications within a specific IP space. Part of the IP space identity triple with ip_space_id_application_name and ip_space_id_resource_type.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpClassification.protocol
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Classification Protocol
dimensions.description: The IP protocol version, ip4 for IPv4 or ip6 for IPv6. Use when filtering classifications by protocol or comparing IPv4 vs. IPv6 classification issues.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpClassification.comment
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Classification Comment
dimensions.description: User-provided description for the classified address (0-1024 characters, UTF-8). Use when searching classifications by address description or notes.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpClassification.mac_address
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Classification Mac Address
dimensions.description: The hardware address of the client involved in the DHCP lease, and the field to use when a question asks which devices are affected. Absent values are an empty string rather than NULL, so use notEquals "" rather than `set`; the placeholder 00:00:00:00:00:00 also occurs.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpClassification.client_id
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Classification Client ID
dimensions.description: The DHCP client identifier, when the lease carried one. Absent values are stored as an empty string rather than NULL, so the `set` operator matches every row and tells you nothing; use notEquals "" to select rows that carry a value. This field can also hold the placeholder 00:00:00:00:00:00. For device identity, prefer mac_address.
dimensions.ai_context: Do not use `set` on this field to mean 'has a client id'. Empty strings are not NULL.

meta.ai_context: Do not use `set` on this field to mean 'has a client id'. Empty strings are not NULL.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpClassification.usage
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Classification Usage
dimensions.description: How the flagged address is being used, in title case: Fixed Address, Reservation, Abandoned. Matching is case-sensitive, so a lower-case value matches nothing. The classifier only fires on these usage types, so a breakdown by this field is the same breakdown as by classification_display with different labels, and a filter for a leased or active address matches nothing here even when such addresses exist in IPAM.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpClassification.classification
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Classification Classification
dimensions.description: The raw DHCP anomaly classification type. The pipeline recognises STALE_RESERVATION (reservation not in asset inventory), STALE_FIXED_ADDRESS (fixed address not in asset inventory with no recent lease), ROGUE_ASSIGNMENT (lease abandoned by client) and RAPID_REQUEST. Which of these are present is data-dependent, so group by this field before filtering on a value: a value that is not present matches zero rows and reads as 'no problems found'. For display labels use classification_display.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpClassification.tags_str
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Classification Tags Str
dimensions.description: Tags on the flagged address, rendered as a comma-separated key-value string. The key order is not stable between rows, because the underlying value is a serialised map, so an equals match against a whole tag string will miss rows carrying the same tags in a different order. Use the contains operator against a single 'key':'value' fragment instead; an object brought in by NIOS federation, for example, is marked with the fragment 'nios/imported':'true'.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpClassification.provider
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Classification Provider
dimensions.description: The raw DDI or cloud provider name for the flagged address, for example bloxone_ddi or nios_ddi. For human-readable names use provider_display, which is derived from this field in the database and cannot disagree with it.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpClassification.service_instance
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Classification Service Instance
dimensions.description: The DHCP service instance assigned to the subnet or range, or the server that detected a rapid request. This field can be blank, and the blank rows collapse into a single unlabelled bucket that can outrank every named server, so exclude them with notEquals "" before ranking DHCP servers. Names appear in two styles, a display name such as 'DHCP xaas-pune' and a hostname such as 'dhcp_host01.example.com', sometimes with an IP appended.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpClassification.ha_group
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Classification Ha Group
dimensions.description: The name of the HA (high availability) group assigned to the subnet or range. Use when filtering classifications by HA group or identifying classifications served by redundant DHCP configurations.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpClassification.access_view_id
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Classification Access View ID
dimensions.description: The reference ID of the access view associated with the subnet containing the classified address. Use when looking up a specific access view by ID or filtering by access view.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpClassification.access_view_name
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Classification Access View Name
dimensions.description: The name of the access view associated with the subnet. Defaults to 'Unassigned' when none is set, so this field can be the same value on every row and yield a group-by of size one.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpClassification.generated_at
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Classification Generated at
dimensions.description: When the classifier last evaluated this address, in whole seconds. Not when the anomaly began, and not when the row was ingested. This is the cube's only time dimension, and it does not work as one: a dateRange placed on it in time_dimensions is accepted and then silently ignored, and a requested granularity produces no time column. Pass no time dimension at all; the cube is already scoped to the last 24 hours. Where an explicit bound is genuinely needed, this field does work in filters with the inDateRange operator. Because the cube keeps only the last 24 hours, an address drops out 24 hours after its last evaluation rather than when its problem is fixed.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpClassification.classification_display
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Classification Classification Display
dimensions.description: Human-readable label for the classification type: Stale Reservations, Stale Fixed Addresses, Rogue Assignments, Rapid Requests. Derived in the database from classification, so the two can never disagree. Which labels are present is data-dependent; group by this field before filtering on one.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpClassification.provider_display
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Classification Provider Display
dimensions.description: Human-readable platform name: NIOS-X for bloxone_ddi, NIOS for nios_ddi, plus AWS, GCP and Azure for the cloud providers. Filter this field with equals, not contains: NIOS is a prefix of NIOS-X, so a contains filter for NIOS also matches every NIOS-X row and silently returns the whole population. Derived in the database from provider, so the two cannot disagree. This field is the platform an object is managed by; it is not the same question as whether an object was imported from a NIOS grid, which is recorded in tags_str.

measures.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpClassification.count
measures.title: Network Insights Dhcp Classification Count
measures.description: Number of classification rows matching the filters. Because the cube keeps exactly one row per address-classification pair, this is identical to count_occurrences in every query; the two are not alternatives. Use count_uniq for the number of distinct affected addresses.

measures.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpClassification.count_uniq
measures.title: Network Insights Dhcp Classification Count Uniq
measures.description: Number of distinct addresses with at least one classification. This is the only one of the three measures that can differ from the others, and it does so when a single address is flagged with more than one anomaly type.

measures.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpClassification.count_occurrences
measures.title: Network Insights Dhcp Classification Count Occurrences
measures.description: Number of distinct address-classification pairs. Identical to count in every query, because the cube already holds exactly one row per pair. Use count_uniq for the number of distinct affected addresses.

full.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpUtilization
full.title: Network Insights Dhcp Utilization
full.description: Per-range DHCP address utilization for the account: one row per DHCP range, carrying its total, used, free, static, dynamic and abandoned address counts, its utilization percentage and utilization tier, plus the range's name, start and end addresses, IP space, parent subnet, DHCP server or HA group, provider, access view, tags and comment. This is a CURRENT SNAPSHOT with no history: the underlying query keeps only the newest row per range from a 24-48 hour window, so utilization trends over time cannot be produced here even though the source table retains 13 months. Ranges deleted upstream are absent entirely. COVERAGE IS NOT GUARANTEED TO BE COMPLETE: IPv6 DHCP ranges have been observed present in the IPAM range data and absent from this cube, so a query here returning no IPv6 ranges does not establish that none are configured. Cross-check IPv6 questions against the IPAM range data. Individual lease records and lease start, expiry or renewal times are not here. Per-address DHCP anomalies are in NetworkInsightsDhcpClassification; subnet and address-block level utilization are in NetworkInsightsSubnetUtilization and NetworkInsightsAddressBlock.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpUtilization.account_id
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Utilization Account ID
dimensions.description: Internal tenant identifier for the CSP account, automatically filtered by the platform's security context. Primary key for row uniqueness. Use when grouping utilization data by tenant account.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpUtilization.ref_id_application_name
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Utilization Ref ID Application Name
dimensions.description: Application identifier for the DHCP range resource. Part of the range identity triple with ref_id_resource_type and ref_id_resource_id. Use when filtering ranges by originating application.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpUtilization.ref_id_resource_type
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Utilization Ref ID Resource Type
dimensions.description: Application-specific type name of the range resource. Part of the range identity triple with ref_id_application_name and ref_id_resource_id. Use when filtering ranges by resource type.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpUtilization.ref_id_resource_id
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Utilization Ref ID Resource ID
dimensions.description: Unique resource identity of the DHCP range, and THE ONLY DIMENSION THAT IDENTIFIES A ROW. Include it whenever you select a utilization number and intend one row per range, or plan to total the result. Distinct count here equals the `count` measure exactly; address_range, start, end and composite_text all return fewer distinct values than there are ranges.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpUtilization.ref_name
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Utilization Ref Name
dimensions.description: Human-readable name of the DHCP range. Blank on any range where no name was set, and the blank is an empty string rather than a null. To count named ranges filter `notEquals` with an empty string; to count unnamed ones filter `equals` with an empty string. Do NOT use `set` or `notSet` here: `set` matches every range including the unnamed ones, which yields the false answer that every range is named. Because a name may be absent, it is not a reliable way to locate a specific range - use ref_id_resource_id or address_range.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpUtilization.start
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Utilization Start
dimensions.description: Start IP address of the DHCP range. For the combined boundary display, use address_range instead. Use when filtering by a specific range start address.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpUtilization.end
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Utilization End
dimensions.description: End IP address of the DHCP range. For the combined boundary display, use address_range instead. Use when filtering by a specific range end address.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpUtilization.protocol
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Utilization Protocol
dimensions.description: IP protocol version of the range. IPv6 RANGES ARE NOT GUARANTEED TO REACH THIS CUBE: they have been observed present in the IPAM range data and absent here, so a `protocol == ip6` filter returning zero rows does NOT establish that no IPv6 DHCP ranges are configured. Never answer 'you have no IPv6 DHCP ranges' from this cube alone. For any IPv6 question, cross-check the IPAM range data (Ipamsvc GET /ipam/range), which carries IPv6 ranges together with a separate IPv6 utilization object, and say which source you used. Any account-wide total computed here should be qualified as covering the ranges this cube received.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpUtilization.comment
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Utilization Comment
dimensions.description: User-provided description for the range; blank when none was set. To find ranges with or without a comment use `equals` or `notEquals` with an empty string rather than `set` or `notSet`, which match every row and no row respectively because the blank is an empty string rather than a null.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpUtilization.space_id_application_name
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Utilization Space ID Application Name
dimensions.description: Application identifier for the IP space containing this range. Part of the IP space identity triple with space_id_resource_type and space_id_resource_id. For the space display name, use space_name. Use when filtering by IP space application.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpUtilization.space_id_resource_type
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Utilization Space ID Resource Type
dimensions.description: Resource type of the IP space containing this range. Part of the IP space identity triple with space_id_application_name and space_id_resource_id. Use when filtering by IP space resource type.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpUtilization.space_id_resource_id
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Utilization Space ID Resource ID
dimensions.description: Unique resource identity of the IP space containing this range. Primary key component. Part of the IP space identity triple. For the space display name, use space_name. Use when querying ranges within a specific IP space.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpUtilization.space_name
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Utilization Space Name
dimensions.description: Display name of the IP space containing this range, already resolved, so grouping on it answers 'how many DHCP ranges are in each IP space' without a separate lookup. For the IP space ID use space_id_resource_id.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpUtilization.parent_application_name
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Utilization Parent Application Name
dimensions.description: Application identifier of the parent subnet for this range. Part of the parent subnet identity triple with parent_resource_type and parent_resource_id. Use when filtering by the parent subnet's application.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpUtilization.parent_resource_type
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Utilization Parent Resource Type
dimensions.description: Resource type of the parent subnet for this range. Part of the parent subnet identity triple with parent_application_name and parent_resource_id. Use when filtering by parent subnet resource type.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpUtilization.parent_resource_id
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Utilization Parent Resource ID
dimensions.description: Unique resource identity of the parent subnet for this range. Part of the parent subnet identity triple with parent_application_name and parent_resource_type. Use when looking up ranges belonging to a specific subnet.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpUtilization.tags_str
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Utilization Tags Str
dimensions.description: Range tags flattened to a comma-separated 'key':'value' string. THE KEY ORDER IS NOT STABLE, so ranges carrying an identical set of tags can render as several different strings and a group-by on this field splits one logical tag set into several groups. Match a single 'key':'value' pair with `contains` instead; an equals comparison against a whole tag string matches only the subset that happens to share that ordering.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpUtilization.disable_dhcp
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Utilization Disable Dhcp
dimensions.description: Whether DHCP is disabled for this range: true means disabled, false means active. Boolean; filter with the strings 'true' or 'false'. Use it to answer 'which ranges have DHCP switched off', and to exclude disabled ranges from utilization analysis.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpUtilization.dhcp_host_id_application_name
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Utilization Dhcp Host ID Application Name
dimensions.description: Application identifier of the DHCP host or HA group serving this range. Part of the DHCP host identity triple with dhcp_host_id_resource_type and dhcp_host_id_resource_id. Use when filtering by DHCP host application.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpUtilization.dhcp_host_id_resource_type
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Utilization Dhcp Host ID Resource Type
dimensions.description: Whether the range is served by a standalone host or an HA group: 'host', 'ha_group', or an empty string when the range has NO DHCP server of either kind. This is the cleanest way to answer 'are any ranges not attached to a DHCP server' - group on it, or filter `equals` with an empty string. Do not use `notSet`, which matches nothing because the blank value is an empty string.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpUtilization.dhcp_host_id_resource_id
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Utilization Dhcp Host ID Resource ID
dimensions.description: Unique resource identity of the DHCP host or HA group serving this range. Part of the DHCP host identity triple with dhcp_host_id_application_name and dhcp_host_id_resource_type. Use when looking up ranges served by a specific DHCP host or HA group.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpUtilization.service_instance
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Utilization Service Instance
dimensions.description: Name of the standalone DHCP server serving this range. Populated only when the range is served by a dhcp/host; when it is served by an HA group this is blank and the name is in ha_group, and a range may have neither, so a breakdown by DHCP server does not necessarily cover every range. Blanks are empty strings, not nulls: to find ranges with no server filter `equals` with an empty string, or group by dhcp_host_id_resource_type. `notSet` matches nothing here.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpUtilization.ha_group
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Utilization Ha Group
dimensions.description: Name of the high-availability group serving this range. Populated only when the range is served by a dhcp/ha_group; when it is served by a standalone host this is blank and the name is in service_instance. Blanks are empty strings, not nulls: to find ranges with no HA group filter `equals` with an empty string, not `notSet`, which matches nothing here.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpUtilization.source
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Utilization Source
dimensions.description: Where the range was discovered or created. GROUP BY THIS DIMENSION BEFORE FILTERING IT, because the value set is data-dependent and an invented value matches zero rows and then gets reported as an absence.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpUtilization.provider
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Utilization Provider
dimensions.description: Cloud or DDI provider for the range. Use when filtering or grouping ranges by provider to compare utilization across providers.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpUtilization.access_view_id
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Utilization Access View ID
dimensions.description: Reference ID of the access view associated with the range. For the display name, use access_view_name. Use when looking up a specific access view by ID.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpUtilization.access_view_name
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Utilization Access View Name
dimensions.description: Display name of the access view associated with the range; defaults to 'Unassigned' if none is set. For the access view ID, use access_view_id. Use when grouping or filtering ranges by access view.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpUtilization.utilization_total
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Utilization Utilization Total
dimensions.description: Total number of IP addresses in the range. DIMENSION, not a measure: placing it in `measures` returns HTTP 400. Denominator for utilization_used, utilization_free and the other counts. To total capacity across ranges, select it together with ref_id_resource_id and sum the returned rows.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpUtilization.utilization_used
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Utilization Utilization Used
dimensions.description: Number of IP addresses currently in use in the range. Equals utilization_static plus utilization_dynamic. DIMENSION, not a measure: placing it in `measures` returns HTTP 400. To total addresses in use across the account, select it together with ref_id_resource_id and sum the rows; selecting it alone groups by distinct value and under-counts badly.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpUtilization.utilization_free
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Utilization Utilization Free
dimensions.description: Number of free IP addresses in the range. Equals utilization_total minus utilization_used. DIMENSION, not a measure: placing it in `measures` returns HTTP 400. To answer 'total free addresses across all my ranges', select it TOGETHER WITH ref_id_resource_id and sum the rows: on its own it groups by distinct value and returns far fewer rows than the account has ranges. This is a per-range COUNT; it does not tell you WHICH addresses are free, which needs the IPAM address data.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpUtilization.utilization_utilization
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Utilization Utilization Utilization
dimensions.description: Percentage of used addresses relative to total in the range, 0-100. DIMENSION, not a measure: placing it in `measures` returns HTTP 400. ALREADY TRUNCATED TO A WHOLE NUMBER upstream, so it can disagree by up to a point with static_utilization, free_utilization and dhcp_utilization, which are computed at full precision. Filter it for arbitrary thresholds: gt, gte, lt and lte all work. 'Over 80%' means gt 80; 'at least 80%' means gte 80. For bucketed tiers use percentage_bucket. There is no average measure, so to compare average utilization across providers select provider plus this plus ref_id_resource_id and average the returned rows.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpUtilization.utilization_abandoned
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Utilization Utilization Abandoned
dimensions.description: Number of IP addresses in the abandoned state, issued by DHCP and then declined by the client. Subset of utilization_dynamic. DIMENSION, not a measure: placing it in `measures` returns HTTP 400. A zero result means no range matched, which is a legitimate answer - report that none were found rather than treating it as a query error or retrying with invented values. For abandoned as a percentage use utilization_abandon_utilization.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpUtilization.utilization_abandon_utilization
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Utilization Utilization Abandon Utilization
dimensions.description: Percentage of abandoned addresses relative to total in the range. DIMENSION, not a measure: placing it in `measures` returns HTTP 400. Like utilization_utilization it arrives already truncated to a whole number. For the raw count use utilization_abandoned.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpUtilization.utilization_dynamic
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Utilization Utilization Dynamic
dimensions.description: Number of IP addresses handed out by DHCP (leases, fixed addresses, abandoned leases). Counterpart to utilization_static. DIMENSION, not a measure: placing it in `measures` returns HTTP 400. For dynamic as a percentage of total use dhcp_utilization. This is an aggregate count, not a list of leases. Pair with ref_id_resource_id before totalling.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpUtilization.utilization_static
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Utilization Utilization Static
dimensions.description: Number of statically defined IP addresses (reservations, fixed addresses, DNS records). Equals utilization_used minus utilization_dynamic. DIMENSION, not a measure: placing it in `measures` returns HTTP 400. For static as a percentage of total use static_utilization. Pair with ref_id_resource_id before totalling.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpUtilization.created_at
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Utilization Created at
dimensions.description: Timestamp when the range was created. Unlike generated_at this is REAL HISTORY and a date range does bind on it, reaching back years, so it answers 'which ranges were created recently'. No range wider than 400 days is accepted. For the last modification use updated_at.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpUtilization.updated_at
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Utilization Updated at
dimensions.description: Timestamp when the range was last modified; equals created_at if never changed. Unlike generated_at this is REAL HISTORY and a date range does bind on it, so it answers 'which ranges changed recently'. No range wider than 400 days is accepted. Note this tracks changes to the range OBJECT, not movement in its utilization, which has no history here.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpUtilization.generated_at
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Utilization Generated at
dimensions.description: Event time at which the upstream system produced this snapshot row, not the time it was ingested. NOT USABLE AS A TIME DIMENSION: placing it in `time_dimensions` causes the date range to be accepted and then ignored, so the result is silently unfiltered, and a granularity produces no time bucket. Filter it as an ordinary member instead, where beforeDate and afterDate work correctly. Because the cube keeps only the newest row per range, every value here falls on the current day; refresh times are staggered per range rather than being one batch.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpUtilization.generated_at_day_ts
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Utilization Generated at Day Ts
dimensions.description: Day-truncated snapshot date. Usable in `time_dimensions` with an explicit range, or as a plain group-by, but NOT in an ordinary `filters` clause, where an equals comparison returns HTTP 400. A relative 'last N days' range ends at the close of the PREVIOUS UTC day, so it silently drops every row stamped in the current UTC day - sometimes all of them, sometimes some. Use 'today', 'this week', or an explicit start and end. No range wider than 400 days is accepted.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpUtilization.operation
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Utilization Operation
dimensions.description: Lifecycle event that produced this row. The values that can appear are 'create', 'update' and 'bootstrap_update'; 'delete' and 'bootstrap_delete' are removed by the cube's own filter and can never be seen, so deleted ranges are absent entirely and questions about removals cannot be answered from this cube.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpUtilization.percentage_bucket
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Utilization Percentage Bucket
dimensions.description: Utilization grouped into labelled tiers. The values are '0-20%', '20-40%', '40-60%', '60-80%', '80-100%', and 'unknown' when utilization falls outside 0-100. Boundaries are EXCLUSIVE AT THE LOWER EDGE, so '80-100%' means strictly greater than 80. Use this for tier distributions; for any other threshold filter utilization_utilization directly.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpUtilization.static_utilization
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Utilization Static Utilization
dimensions.description: Percentage of total addresses that are statically defined. Computed in the cube at full precision, unlike utilization_utilization which is a whole number. DIMENSION, not a measure: placing it in `measures` returns HTTP 400. For the raw count use utilization_static.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpUtilization.free_utilization
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Utilization Free Utilization
dimensions.description: Percentage of total addresses that are free. Computed in the cube at full precision, unlike utilization_utilization which is a whole number. DIMENSION, not a measure: placing it in `measures` returns HTTP 400. For the raw count use utilization_free.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpUtilization.dhcp_utilization
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Utilization Dhcp Utilization
dimensions.description: Percentage of total addresses handed out by DHCP. Computed in the cube at full precision, unlike utilization_utilization which is a whole number. DIMENSION, not a measure: placing it in `measures` returns HTTP 400. For the raw count use utilization_dynamic.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpUtilization.address_range
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Utilization Address Range
dimensions.description: The DHCP range as "start - end" (e.g. "10.0.0.1 - 10.0.0.254"). Human-readable and good for display, but NOT UNIQUE: ranges can share an identical start-end string, so grouping on it silently merges them and a total summed from it is short. Use ref_id_resource_id as the row key and carry this alongside for labelling.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpUtilization.composite_text
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Utilization Composite Text
dimensions.description: Concatenated search field built from start, end, ref_name, the utilization percentage and service_instance. Because it embeds a number it will also match numeric search terms, and where ref_name is blank it contains a gap in place of the name. Not unique, so it is not a row key.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpUtilization.synthetic_monitor_ts
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dhcp Utilization Synthetic Monitor Ts
dimensions.description: Alias of generated_at intended for monitoring dashboards. Behaves like generated_at_day_ts rather than like generated_at: it does accept a range in `time_dimensions`, but a relative 'last N days' range silently drops rows stamped in the current UTC day. Prefer generated_at_day_ts for day grouping.

measures.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpUtilization.count
measures.title: Network Insights Dhcp Utilization Count
measures.description: Number of DHCP ranges matching the filters. THE DEFAULT MEASURE: use it for every 'how many', 'which', 'list' and 'rank' question, including per-range listings, where the per-range values come from the DIMENSIONS and count simply accompanies them. It counts RANGES and never sums addresses, which are dimensions. Use it to sanity-check any per-range result: if a query returned fewer rows than count reports, the group-by collapsed rows and any total from it is wrong.

measures.name: NetworkInsightsDhcpUtilization.percent
measures.title: Network Insights Dhcp Utilization Percent
measures.description: Share of the range count that the current group represents, already expressed as a percentage. It is a share of the rows THE CURRENT FILTERS SELECT, not of every range in the account, so under a filter it renormalises to 100 across the filtered set. Use it only when the question explicitly asks for a percentage, share or proportion OF RANGES, and use it directly rather than computing the percentage from count. Like count it measures RANGES, not addresses.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsHostLookup.host_id
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Host Lookup Host ID

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsHostLookup.host_name
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Host Lookup Host Name

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsHostLookup.timestamp
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Host Lookup Timestamp

full.name: NetworkInsightsDnsHostLookup
full.title: Network Insights Dns Host Lookup
full.description: One row per DNS host observed answering DNS queries within the retained window, derived from DNS query logs rather than from configuration. Retains roughly one day, so it holds no history and cannot show a trend; a requested range wider than a day returns the same rows rather than an error. A configured DNS server that served no query in the window does not appear at all, so a row count here is not a count of DNS servers: on a probed account this cube held 39 hosts while the DNS host configuration API held 61, the difference being external DNS providers, idle or erroring appliances, and grid members whose logs do not reach this pipeline. Has no measures: count hosts by reading rows. Carries no IP address, site, location, client identity or query-volume field.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsHostLookup.host_id
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Host Lookup Host ID
dimensions.description: Identifier of the DNS host that reported the query, and the primary key of this lookup. This is the platform's on-prem host identifier (ophid), so the same value appears as the ophid field on the DNS host configuration and Infrastructure host records, which is the practical way to carry a result from here into configuration or inventory data. A host_id that exists in configuration can legitimately return no row here.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsHostLookup.host_name
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Host Lookup Host Name
dimensions.description: Name of the DNS host, carried through unchanged from the administrator-configured DNS host name, so it matches the name shown in DNS host configuration exactly. Configured names frequently embed an IP address after whitespace, and the internal spacing is irregular, so an exact match on a bare hostname or FQDN can return nothing while the host exists. Match with contains rather than equals, and note that contains ignores case. For the same reason an endsWith match on a domain suffix misses any host whose name has anything appended after it.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsHostLookup.timestamp
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Host Lookup Timestamp
dimensions.description: Event time of the most recent DNS query this host reported, which makes it effectively a last-seen-answering-queries time rather than a metadata refresh time. Whole-second precision. The value comes from the reporting appliance's own clock and can run a few minutes ahead of the present, so a window whose upper bound is exactly now can omit the newest rows; extend the upper bound past now, or omit the range, to see them all.

full.ai_context: DDI/Network Insights domain. Use it to resolve a DNS host identifier to a name, and to find when a host was last seen answering DNS queries. For a count or inventory of configured DNS servers, use the DNS host configuration API or the Infrastructure services inventory instead, because this cube only sees hosts that carried traffic. For DNS failures broken down by server, use NetworkInsightsDnsRawLogs, which already exposes the server name directly and needs no lookup from here. For a host's IP address, site or location, use the Infrastructure host inventory. For current query rate, use host service metrics. Absence of a host from this cube is not evidence that the host is idle or misconfigured, only that no DNS query from it reached this pipeline in the window.

meta.ai_context: DDI/Network Insights domain. Use it to resolve a DNS host identifier to a name, and to find when a host was last seen answering DNS queries. For a count or inventory of configured DNS servers, use the DNS host configuration API or the Infrastructure services inventory instead, because this cube only sees hosts that carried traffic. For DNS failures broken down by server, use NetworkInsightsDnsRawLogs, which already exposes the server name directly and needs no lookup from here. For a host's IP address, site or location, use the Infrastructure host inventory. For current query rate, use host service metrics. Absence of a host from this cube is not evidence that the host is idle or misconfigured, only that no DNS query from it reached this pipeline in the window.

full.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRawLogs
full.title: Network Insights Dns Raw Logs
full.description: Failed DNS transactions only, one row per failed event. Retains roughly three days. Successful lookups are not stored here, so this cube can tell you what is failing and where, but never total query volume, a success count, or a failure rate.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRawLogs.qname
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Raw Logs Qname
dimensions.description: The fully qualified domain name that failed to resolve. Values repeat heavily - a single busy name can account for a large share of a day's rows - so this is a grouping dimension, not a unique row key, despite being declared a primary key.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRawLogs.timestamp
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Raw Logs Timestamp
dimensions.description: Event time reported by the DNS server, to whole-second precision. Every query must supply an explicit range on this dimension or it is rejected. Only about the last three days are retained.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRawLogs.view_id
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Raw Logs View ID
dimensions.description: Identifier of the DNS view. Not always a UUID: appliance-style names such as _default and _bind also appear, and those are among the values the name dictionary cannot resolve. A blank means no view was recorded on the row.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRawLogs.view_name
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Raw Logs View Name
dimensions.description: DNS view name, resolved through a lookup dictionary rather than stored on the row. It is blank both for rows that carried no view and for rows whose view identifier is not in the dictionary, so a blank does not mean the query had no view. Group by view_id as well before concluding a view is missing, and report the blank group rather than dropping it.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRawLogs.classification
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Raw Logs Classification
dimensions.description: String form of the response code, such as NXDOMAIN, SERVFAIL, REFUSED or NOTAUTH. NOERROR never appears, because successful transactions are not stored. It arrives as its own field rather than being derived from the numeric code. Which values are present is data-dependent, so group by this dimension before filtering on a particular one.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRawLogs.server_id
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Raw Logs Server ID
dimensions.description: Identifier of the DNS server that answered. This is the responding server, not the requesting client; this cube carries no client identity of any kind.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRawLogs.server_name
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Raw Logs Server Name
dimensions.description: Name of the DNS server that answered - not the client that asked. Resolved through a lookup dictionary. Some names have an IP address appended after whitespace, so prefer contains over equals when matching a hostname.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRawLogs.qtype
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Raw Logs Qtype
dimensions.description: DNS record type requested, as a string, for example A, AAAA, PTR, SRV, SOA or HTTPS. Reverse-lookup PTR failures and forward A/AAAA failures have different causes, so keep them separate rather than reporting one failure total.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRawLogs.rcode
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Raw Logs Rcode
dimensions.description: Numeric DNS response code. Response code 0 (NOERROR) never appears here, because successful transactions are filtered out before storage; a filter for 0 returns an empty result rather than an error. The values present are failure codes such as 2 SERVFAIL, 3 NXDOMAIN, 5 REFUSED and 9 NOTAUTH. Which of them are present is data-dependent, so group by this dimension before filtering on a particular code.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRawLogs.zone_id
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Raw Logs Zone ID
dimensions.description: Identifier of the DNS zone. The empty string is a real stored value meaning the failure carries no zone attribution, and it can be the largest group; exclude it explicitly when you want only named zones.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRawLogs.zone_name
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Raw Logs Zone Name
dimensions.description: Zone FQDN, resolved through a lookup dictionary. Values carry a trailing dot, so an equals filter on the bare name matches nothing; prefer contains. Blank means the failure was not attributed to any zone, and that blank group can be larger than all the named zones put together.

measures.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRawLogs.count
measures.title: Network Insights Dns Raw Logs Count
measures.description: Number of failed DNS transactions matching the filters. This is a count of failures, not of queries: successful lookups are not stored, so it can never serve as the denominator of a failure rate.

measures.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRawLogs.unique_zone_count
measures.title: Network Insights Dns Raw Logs Unique Zone Count
measures.description: Number of distinct zone identifiers in the filtered rows. It counts the no-zone bucket as one additional zone, so subtract one if you need only named zones, and say how much of the failure volume carries no zone at all.

measures.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRawLogs.unique_server_count
measures.title: Network Insights Dns Raw Logs Unique Server Count
measures.description: Number of distinct DNS servers in the filtered rows. Grouping this by zone is the useful pairing: it shows whether a zone is failing on one server or across many, which a separate server total and zone total cannot show.

full.ai_context: SCOPE: only DNS transactions that returned a non-zero response code are stored; the ingest view filters out every successful lookup. A count here is a count of failures, never of queries, and a filter for a successful response code returns an empty result rather than an error. WINDOW: roughly three days. A 7-day or 30-day request returns the same three days with no warning, and a window older than that returns no rows rather than an error, so an empty result means the data has expired, not that nothing failed. A requested span wider than 66 days is rejected, and every query must carry an explicit time range. NO CLIENT IDENTITY: no client IP, MAC, hostname or site; the server fields identify the DNS server that answered, not the device that asked. FIELD NAMES: server_name and server_id, view_name and view_id, zone_name and zone_id, qname, qtype, rcode, classification. There is no 'server', 'dns_view', 'response_code' or 'hour_of_day' field; for an hourly shape use a time dimension with hour granularity. DDI/Network Insights domain — DNS service health, not security. Use it for DNS resolution failures, response-code and error-pattern analysis, and query-type breakdowns per server, zone or view. Despite the name, 'Network Insights' is unrelated to Threat Defense insights: this cube holds no security actions, threat indicators, severities or enforcement outcomes. For any question about security events, blocked versus unblocked DNS activity, threat feeds, threat actors, or insights, use SecurityActionSummaryView, SecurityActionIndicators or SecurityActionAssets — or PortunusRawRpzLogs_ch_s for raw RPZ enforcement events.

meta.ai_context: SCOPE: only DNS transactions that returned a non-zero response code are stored; the ingest view filters out every successful lookup. A count here is a count of failures, never of queries, and a filter for a successful response code returns an empty result rather than an error. WINDOW: roughly three days. A 7-day or 30-day request returns the same three days with no warning, and a window older than that returns no rows rather than an error, so an empty result means the data has expired, not that nothing failed. A requested span wider than 66 days is rejected, and every query must carry an explicit time range. NO CLIENT IDENTITY: no client IP, MAC, hostname or site; the server fields identify the DNS server that answered, not the device that asked. FIELD NAMES: server_name and server_id, view_name and view_id, zone_name and zone_id, qname, qtype, rcode, classification. There is no 'server', 'dns_view', 'response_code' or 'hour_of_day' field; for an hourly shape use a time dimension with hour granularity. DDI/Network Insights domain — DNS service health, not security. Use it for DNS resolution failures, response-code and error-pattern analysis, and query-type breakdowns per server, zone or view. Despite the name, 'Network Insights' is unrelated to Threat Defense insights: this cube holds no security actions, threat indicators, severities or enforcement outcomes. For any question about security events, blocked versus unblocked DNS activity, threat feeds, threat actors, or insights, use SecurityActionSummaryView, SecurityActionIndicators or SecurityActionAssets — or PortunusRawRpzLogs_ch_s for raw RPZ enforcement events.

full.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecords
full.title: Network Insights Dns Records
full.description: DNS record insight violation events showing which DNS records currently violate asset insight indicators. One row per violated indicator rule per DNS record, with severity, confidence, and acknowledgment status. Use for questions about DNS hygiene issues, stale records, violation counts by zone, provider, record type, or severity. For one row per unique DNS record with aggregated indicator lists, use NetworkInsightsDnsRecordsRolledByIndicatorId instead. Supports filtering by indicator, severity, zone, provider, record type, and acknowledgment status.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecords.account_id
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Account ID
dimensions.description: Internal tenant identifier (UUID) automatically filtered by the platform's security context. Each query is scoped to a single tenant. Use when grouping insight violations by tenant account. For the DNS record's own account, use record_asset_account_id.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecords.insight_type
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Insight Type
dimensions.description: The broad category of asset insight. A single constant value for this cube, so grouping by it separates nothing. For the category of an individual finding use indicator_id.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecords.indicator_id
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Indicator ID
dimensions.description: The category of the finding, carrying readable names rather than opaque identifiers. This is the dimension that says what KIND of problem a record has, with values such as Stale, Dangling and Untrusted. Group by it to discover which categories are present before filtering on one, since an invented value matches no rows and gets reported as none found. Do not look for the finding category in insight_subclassification or severity.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecords.indicator_rule_id
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Indicator Rule ID
dimensions.description: The unique identifier of a specific rule within an indicator. An indicator may have multiple rules with different conditions. Use when drilling into specific rules that triggered violations. For indicator-level grouping, use indicator_id.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecords.provider
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Provider
dimensions.description: The cloud or DDI provider associated with the insight event at the event level. Use when filtering or grouping violations by event-level provider. For the DNS record's own provider list, use record_asset_provider_types_str for display or record_asset_provider_types for raw values.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecords.state
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records State
dimensions.description: The lifecycle state of the finding. May carry no value, in which case filtering on a state name such as active or acknowledged matches no rows and returns a misleading zero. Group by it before filtering on it.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecords.ack_user_id
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Ack User ID
dimensions.description: Who acknowledged the finding, empty when nobody has. May be empty throughout, in which case no acknowledgment analysis is possible.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecords.confidence_level
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Confidence Level
dimensions.description: The confidence of the evaluation. May hold a single constant value, in which case it cannot rank or separate findings.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecords.severity
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Severity
dimensions.description: The severity assigned by the indicator definition. May carry no value, in which case filtering on a severity name matches no rows and a severity breakdown returns a single empty bucket. Group by it to confirm it is populated before filtering or before offering a severity breakdown; to prioritise findings use indicator_id instead.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecords.violated
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Violated
dimensions.description: Always true here, because the cube contains only violations. It cannot be used to find compliant records.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecords.record_asset_id
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Record Asset ID
dimensions.description: Primary key identifying the DNS record being evaluated, as assigned by BloxOne DDI. Use when looking up a specific DNS record, joining with other record data, or deduplicating results by record.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecords.record_asset_name
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Record Asset Name
dimensions.description: The DNS record's own label within its zone, a short label such as a host name or a reverse-zone octet pair, not a fully qualified name. This is the dimension to use when listing or naming individual records. No dimension holds a record's fully qualified name: build one by joining this label to record_asset_absolute_zone_name.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecords.record_asset_account_id
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Record Asset Account ID
dimensions.description: The account ID associated with the DNS record from its metadata. Typically matches the tenant account_id. Use when filtering records by their owning account. For the tenant-level identifier, use account_id.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecords.record_asset_view_id
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Record Asset View ID
dimensions.description: The DNS view ID for the record. A DNS view controls which records are visible to which clients. Use when filtering or grouping records by DNS view, or joining with NetworkInsightsDnsViewLookup.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecords.record_asset_dns_name
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Record Asset Dns Name
dimensions.description: Despite the name, this carries the ABSOLUTE ZONE NAME rather than the record's own name, and repeats the value in record_asset_absolute_zone_name. Do not use it to list, name or filter individual records: for the record's label use record_asset_name. For grouping or displaying zones, prefer record_asset_absolute_zone_name, which is the canonical zone dimension and the one count_zones counts.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecords.record_asset_record_type
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Record Asset Record Type
dimensions.description: The DNS resource record type. The set present is data-dependent and can include types beyond the common A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, PTR and TXT, such as DHCID, so group by this dimension before filtering on a type.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecords.record_asset_rdata
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Record Asset Rdata
dimensions.description: Stringified JSON of the DNS record data containing the actual record value in structured form. Use when inspecting raw record data for a specific violation. For the DNS wire-format representation, use record_asset_dns_rdata instead.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecords.record_asset_provider_zone_type
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Record Asset Provider Zone Type
dimensions.description: The zone type classification: public, private, or empty. Indicates whether the DNS zone hosting this record is publicly resolvable or internal. Use when filtering DNS records by zone visibility.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecords.record_asset_provider_types
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Record Asset Provider Types
dimensions.description: Raw provider identifiers, returned as an array. This dimension cannot be filtered: any filter on it fails. Group by or filter record_asset_provider_types_str instead.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecords.record_asset_dns_absolute_zone_name
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Record Asset Dns Absolute Zone Name
dimensions.description: Wire-format twin of record_asset_absolute_zone_name, carrying the same zone value. Prefer record_asset_absolute_zone_name for grouping and display.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecords.record_asset_absolute_zone_name
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Record Asset Absolute Zone Name
dimensions.description: The human-readable absolute name of the zone holding the record, with a trailing dot. This is the zone dimension to group or filter by, and the one count_zones counts. Its wire-format twin record_asset_dns_absolute_zone_name carries the same value.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecords.record_asset_comment
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Record Asset Comment
dimensions.description: The administrator-provided description for the DNS record (0-1024 characters, UTF-8). Set by the record owner in BloxOne DDI. Use when searching records by their comment or description text.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecords.record_asset_source
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Record Asset Source
dimensions.description: Raw source indicators, returned as an array. This dimension cannot be filtered: any filter on it fails. Group by or filter record_asset_source_str instead.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecords.record_asset_disabled
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Record Asset Disabled
dimensions.description: Whether the DNS record is disabled in BloxOne DDI. Disabled records are excluded from DNS configuration but may still be evaluated by the insight engine. Use when filtering for active vs. disabled records.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecords.record_asset_compartment_id
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Record Asset Compartment ID
dimensions.description: The compartment (organizational grouping) associated with the DNS record; empty if not assigned to a compartment. Use when filtering records by compartment.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecords.insight_subclassification
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Insight Subclassification
dimensions.description: A finer subclassification within the insight type. May carry no value at all, in which case filtering on it matches no rows and yields a misleading zero. Group by it to confirm it is populated before filtering; for the category of a finding use indicator_id instead.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecords.evaluation_day_ts
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Evaluation Day Ts
dimensions.description: The day an insight was evaluated against the record, and the ONLY time dimension whose requested range is actually applied. Use this one to bound a time range or to bucket by day. Because only the newest evaluation per record is kept, a day breakdown shows when each record was last re-evaluated rather than how many findings arose that day. Findings are re-evaluated in a single daily batch, so the current day's bucket can hold almost nothing while the full retained window holds far more. A range narrowed to the last 24 hours can therefore return zero when findings do exist. Unless the question is about one specific day, bound the range to the whole retained window rather than narrowing it.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecords.evaluation_time
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Evaluation Time
dimensions.description: The timestamp an insight was evaluated against the record. A dateRange supplied for this dimension as a time dimension is accepted but NOT applied, so the result silently covers everything the cube holds: bound a range with evaluation_day_ts instead, or filter this dimension with inDateRange, beforeDate or afterDate. Its comparison and equality operators are all rejected: only inDateRange, beforeDate, afterDate and set work.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecords.ack_time
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Ack Time
dimensions.description: When the finding was acknowledged. Sits at the 1970 epoch when it has never been acknowledged, rather than being empty, so exclude that value when looking for real acknowledgment times.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecords.ack_until_time
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Ack Until Time
dimensions.description: When an acknowledgment expires, after which the finding resurfaces. Sits at the 1970 epoch when the finding has never been acknowledged.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecords.record_asset_last_queried
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Record Asset Last Queried
dimensions.description: When the record was last queried by a resolver. Sits at the 1970 epoch both when the record has never been queried and when any lookup predates the tenant's tracking epoch in record_asset_last_queried_feature_epoch, so it is not a dependable staleness signal on its own. For records Infoblox considers stale, filter indicator_id instead.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecords.record_asset_last_queried_str
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Record Asset Last Queried Str
dimensions.description: Formatted last-queried time, blank where record_asset_last_queried sits at the 1970 epoch. Use for display; use record_asset_last_queried for date filtering.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecords.operation
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Operation
dimensions.description: Not queryable. Grouping by this dimension fails outright, and filtering on it matches no rows and returns zero rather than an error, because it is declared as a time dimension over a non-time value. Do not group by it or filter on it. Records deleted upstream are already excluded from this cube.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecords.record_asset_source_str
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Record Asset Source Str
dimensions.description: Comma-separated indication of how the record was created, with values such as STATIC for records created by hand or via the API, DYNAMIC for DDNS registrations, SYSTEM, DELEGATED and DTC. Use contains rather than equals. The set present is data-dependent, so group by this dimension before filtering on a value.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecords.record_asset_provider_types_str
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Record Asset Provider Types Str
dimensions.description: Comma-separated display names of the platforms hosting the record, with values such as AWS, GCP, Azure, NIOS-X for on-premises Infoblox DDI, and NIOS. Use contains rather than equals, since a record can carry more than one. The set present is data-dependent, so group by this dimension before filtering on a value.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecords.composite_text
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Composite Text
dimensions.description: A concatenation of the record's indicator, name, type, data, providers, zone and last-queried value, for keyword search across all of them. Not useful as a group-by, since it is distinct per row.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecords.record_asset_ttl
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Record Asset Ttl
dimensions.description: The TTL (time-to-live) value in seconds for the DNS record. Determines how long resolvers cache this record. Use when filtering by TTL or finding records with unusually high or low TTL values.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecords.record_asset_tags
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Record Asset Tags
dimensions.description: Raw tag map for the record. Prefer record_asset_tags_str, which is the brace-stripped comma-separated form; both are blank when the record carries no tags.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecords.record_asset_tags_str
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Record Asset Tags Str
dimensions.description: Tags associated with the DNS record as comma-separated key-value pairs. Use when filtering or searching records by custom metadata labels. For raw tag map access, use record_asset_tags instead.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecords.record_asset_dns_rdata
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Record Asset Dns Rdata
dimensions.description: The DNS protocol textual representation of the record data (wire-format). The actual DNS answer content as it would appear in a DNS response. Use when inspecting DNS response data. For JSON-structured record data, use record_asset_rdata instead.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecords.synthetic_monitor_ts
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Synthetic Monitor Ts
dimensions.description: An alias of evaluation_time provided for monitoring dashboards. For ordinary time filtering and bucketing use evaluation_day_ts.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecords.record_asset_last_queried_feature_epoch
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Record Asset Last Queried Feature Epoch
dimensions.description: When last-queried tracking was enabled for the tenant. A lookup before this point is indistinguishable from never having been queried.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecords.record_asset_zone_id
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Record Asset Zone ID
dimensions.description: The zone's identifier. Distinct zone identifiers can outnumber distinct zone names, because the same zone name can exist in more than one DNS view. Group by record_asset_absolute_zone_name for a zone breakdown by name.

measures.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecords.count
measures.title: Network Insights Dns Records Count
measures.description: Number of finding rows, one per violated indicator rule per record. Use for how many findings. It exceeds count_uniq only where a record violates more than one indicator rule, so the two can coincide.

measures.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecords.count_uniq
measures.title: Network Insights Dns Records Count Uniq
measures.description: Number of distinct DNS records with at least one finding, however many indicators each violates. Use for how many records are affected.

measures.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecords.count_occurrences
measures.title: Network Insights Dns Records Count Occurrences
measures.description: Number of distinct record-and-indicator pairs. Coincides with count where each record violates a single rule per indicator.

measures.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecords.count_zones
measures.title: Network Insights Dns Records Count Zones
measures.description: Number of distinct zone NAMES holding at least one flagged record. A zone name present in more than one DNS view is counted once, so this can be lower than the number of distinct zone objects.

measures.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecords.count_providers
measures.title: Network Insights Dns Records Count Providers
measures.description: Number of distinct platforms hosting at least one flagged record.
