full.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecordsRolledByIndicatorId
full.title: Network Insights Dns Records Rolled by Indicator ID
full.description: DNS record hygiene findings rolled up to ONE ROW PER DNS RECORD, carrying the complete list of indicators that record violates. Use this for questions about which DNS records have problems, for listing records together with everything wrong with each one, and for counting how many RECORDS are affected. For a total number of individual findings, where a record with three problems counts as three, use NetworkInsightsDnsRecords, which keeps one row per finding. The category of each finding has readable values such as Stale, Dangling and Untrusted; group by the indicator list to see which are present rather than guessing a value. Contains only records that violate an indicator, so it cannot list compliant records and an empty result does not mean the estate is healthy; for the full DNS record inventory use the DNS record REST collection instead. Holds only the most recent evaluation of each record over a short trailing window, so it is a current-state snapshot rather than a history and cannot support a trend.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecordsRolledByIndicatorId.account_id
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Rolled by Indicator ID Account ID
dimensions.description: Internal tenant identifier (UUID) automatically filtered by the platform's security context. Each query is scoped to a single tenant. Use when grouping insight violations by tenant account. For the DNS record's own account, use record_asset_account_id.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecordsRolledByIndicatorId.insight_type
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Rolled by Indicator ID Insight Type
dimensions.description: The broad category of asset insight. May hold a single constant value, in which case grouping by it separates nothing. For the category of a finding use indicator_ids_str.

meta.description: The broad category of asset insight. May hold a single constant value, in which case grouping by it separates nothing. For the category of a finding use indicator_ids_str.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecordsRolledByIndicatorId.indicator_id
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Rolled by Indicator ID Indicator ID
dimensions.description: The category of only ONE of the record's findings, the one evaluated most recently, because this cube keeps a single row per record. Counting or grouping records by this dimension therefore under-counts every category that shares a record with another category. Do not use it to answer how many records carry a given category, and do not use it for a category breakdown: use indicator_ids_str with contains instead. For per-finding counts by category, use NetworkInsightsDnsRecords.

meta.description: The category of only ONE of the record's findings, the one evaluated most recently, because this cube keeps a single row per record. Counting or grouping records by this dimension therefore under-counts every category that shares a record with another category. Do not use it to answer how many records carry a given category, and do not use it for a category breakdown: use indicator_ids_str with contains instead. For per-finding counts by category, use NetworkInsightsDnsRecords.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecordsRolledByIndicatorId.indicator_rule_id
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Rolled by Indicator ID Indicator Rule ID
dimensions.description: The specific rule behind the single most recently evaluated finding on this record, not behind all of them. It under-counts in the same way indicator_id does. Use indicator_ids_str for a complete view.

meta.description: The specific rule behind the single most recently evaluated finding on this record, not behind all of them. It under-counts in the same way indicator_id does. Use indicator_ids_str for a complete view.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecordsRolledByIndicatorId.provider
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Rolled by Indicator ID Provider
dimensions.description: The platform associated with the most recently evaluated finding on the record. For the record's own hosting platform use record_asset_provider_types_str.

meta.description: The platform associated with the most recently evaluated finding on the record. For the record's own hosting platform use record_asset_provider_types_str.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecordsRolledByIndicatorId.state
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Rolled by Indicator ID State
dimensions.description: The lifecycle state of the most recently evaluated finding on the record. May carry no value, in which case filtering on a state name such as active or acknowledged matches no rows and returns a misleading zero. Group by it before filtering on it.

meta.description: The lifecycle state of the most recently evaluated finding on the record. May carry no value, in which case filtering on a state name such as active or acknowledged matches no rows and returns a misleading zero. Group by it before filtering on it.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecordsRolledByIndicatorId.ack_user_id
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Rolled by Indicator ID Ack User ID
dimensions.description: Who acknowledged the finding, empty when nobody has. May be empty throughout, in which case no acknowledgment analysis is possible.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecordsRolledByIndicatorId.confidence_level
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Rolled by Indicator ID Confidence Level
dimensions.description: The confidence of the evaluation. May hold a single constant value, in which case it cannot rank or separate findings.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecordsRolledByIndicatorId.severity
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Rolled by Indicator ID Severity
dimensions.description: The severity assigned by the indicator definition, and only for the most recently evaluated finding on the record. It may carry no value, in which case filtering on a severity name matches nothing and a severity breakdown returns a single blank bucket. Group by it to confirm it is populated before filtering or before offering a severity breakdown; to prioritise findings use indicator_ids_str.

meta.description: The severity assigned by the indicator definition, and only for the most recently evaluated finding on the record. It may carry no value, in which case filtering on a severity name matches nothing and a severity breakdown returns a single blank bucket. Group by it to confirm it is populated before filtering or before offering a severity breakdown; to prioritise findings use indicator_ids_str.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecordsRolledByIndicatorId.violated
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Rolled by Indicator ID Violated
dimensions.description: Always true here, because the cube contains only violations. It cannot be used to find compliant records.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecordsRolledByIndicatorId.record_asset_id
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Rolled by Indicator ID Record Asset ID
dimensions.description: Primary key identifying the DNS record being evaluated, as assigned by BloxOne DDI. Use when looking up a specific DNS record, joining with other record data, or deduplicating results by record.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecordsRolledByIndicatorId.record_asset_name
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Rolled by Indicator ID Record Asset Name
dimensions.description: The DNS record's own label within its zone: a hostname label, or in a reverse zone a numeric label. This is the dimension to use when listing or naming individual records. No dimension holds a record's fully qualified name: build one by joining this label to record_asset_absolute_zone_name.

meta.description: The DNS record's own label within its zone: a hostname label, or in a reverse zone a numeric label. This is the dimension to use when listing or naming individual records. No dimension holds a record's fully qualified name: build one by joining this label to record_asset_absolute_zone_name.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecordsRolledByIndicatorId.record_asset_account_id
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Rolled by Indicator ID Record Asset Account ID
dimensions.description: The account ID associated with the DNS record from its metadata. Typically matches the tenant account_id. Use when filtering records by their owning account. For the tenant-level identifier, use account_id.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecordsRolledByIndicatorId.record_asset_view_id
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Rolled by Indicator ID Record Asset View ID
dimensions.description: The DNS view ID for the record. A DNS view controls which records are visible to which clients. Use when filtering or grouping records by DNS view, or joining with NetworkInsightsDnsViewLookup.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecordsRolledByIndicatorId.record_asset_dns_name
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Rolled by Indicator ID Record Asset Dns Name
dimensions.description: Despite the name, this carries the ABSOLUTE ZONE NAME rather than the record's own name, and repeats the value in record_asset_absolute_zone_name. Do not use it to list, name or filter individual records: for the record's label use record_asset_name. For grouping or displaying zones, prefer record_asset_absolute_zone_name, which is the canonical zone dimension and the one count_zones counts.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecordsRolledByIndicatorId.record_asset_record_type
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Rolled by Indicator ID Record Asset Record Type
dimensions.description: The DNS resource record type. The set present is data-dependent and can include types beyond the common A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, PTR and TXT, such as DHCID, so group by this dimension before filtering on a type.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecordsRolledByIndicatorId.record_asset_rdata
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Rolled by Indicator ID Record Asset Rdata
dimensions.description: Stringified JSON of the DNS record data containing the actual record value in structured form. Use when inspecting raw record data for a specific violation. For the DNS wire-format representation, use record_asset_dns_rdata instead.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecordsRolledByIndicatorId.record_asset_provider_zone_type
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Rolled by Indicator ID Record Asset Provider Zone Type
dimensions.description: The zone type classification: public, private, or empty. Indicates whether the DNS zone hosting this record is publicly resolvable or internal. Use when filtering DNS records by zone visibility.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecordsRolledByIndicatorId.record_asset_dns_absolute_zone_name
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Rolled by Indicator ID Record Asset Dns Absolute Zone Name
dimensions.description: Wire-format twin of record_asset_absolute_zone_name, carrying the same zone value. Prefer record_asset_absolute_zone_name for grouping and display.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecordsRolledByIndicatorId.record_asset_absolute_zone_name
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Rolled by Indicator ID Record Asset Absolute Zone Name
dimensions.description: The human-readable absolute name of the zone holding the record, with a trailing dot. This is the zone dimension to group or filter by, and the one count_zones counts. Its wire-format twin record_asset_dns_absolute_zone_name carries the same value.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecordsRolledByIndicatorId.record_asset_comment
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Rolled by Indicator ID Record Asset Comment
dimensions.description: The administrator-provided description for the DNS record (0-1024 characters, UTF-8). Set by the record owner in BloxOne DDI. Use when searching records by their comment or description text.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecordsRolledByIndicatorId.record_asset_disabled
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Rolled by Indicator ID Record Asset Disabled
dimensions.description: Whether the DNS record is disabled in BloxOne DDI. Disabled records are excluded from DNS configuration but may still be evaluated by the insight engine. Use when filtering for active vs. disabled records.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecordsRolledByIndicatorId.record_asset_compartment_id
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Rolled by Indicator ID Record Asset Compartment ID
dimensions.description: The compartment (organizational grouping) associated with the DNS record; empty if not assigned to a compartment. Use when filtering records by compartment.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecordsRolledByIndicatorId.insight_subclassification
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Rolled by Indicator ID Insight Subclassification
dimensions.description: A finer subclassification within the insight type, and NOT the category of a finding. It may carry no value at all, in which case filtering it matches nothing and returns a zero that reads as 'no problems of that kind found' when the real number can be in the hundreds. Do not filter or group by it to find stale, dangling or untrusted records: that category is in indicator_ids_str. Group by it first if you want to know whether it is populated.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecordsRolledByIndicatorId.evaluation_day_ts
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Rolled by Indicator ID Evaluation Day Ts
dimensions.description: The day an insight was evaluated against the record, and the ONLY time dimension whose requested range is actually applied. Use this one to bound a time range or to bucket by day. Because only each record's newest evaluation is kept, a day breakdown collapses to the day of the last re-evaluation and shows when records were last checked rather than when problems arose. A requested range far wider than the cube actually holds is accepted without complaint and answered from the short window it scans, so a multi-year request returns the same few days as a multi-day one.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecordsRolledByIndicatorId.evaluation_time
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Rolled by Indicator ID Evaluation Time
dimensions.description: The timestamp an insight was evaluated against the record. A dateRange supplied for this dimension as a time dimension is accepted but NOT applied, so the result silently covers everything the cube holds: bound a range with evaluation_day_ts instead, or filter this dimension with inDateRange, beforeDate or afterDate. Its comparison and equality operators are all rejected: only inDateRange, beforeDate, afterDate and set work.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecordsRolledByIndicatorId.ack_time
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Rolled by Indicator ID Ack Time
dimensions.description: When the finding was acknowledged. Sits at the 1970 epoch when it has never been acknowledged, rather than being empty, so exclude that value when looking for real acknowledgment times.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecordsRolledByIndicatorId.ack_until_time
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Rolled by Indicator ID Ack Until Time
dimensions.description: When an acknowledgment expires, after which the finding resurfaces. Sits at the 1970 epoch when the finding has never been acknowledged.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecordsRolledByIndicatorId.record_asset_last_queried
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Rolled by Indicator ID Record Asset Last Queried
dimensions.description: When the record was last queried by a resolver. Sits at the 1970 epoch both when the record has never been queried and when any lookup predates the tenant's tracking epoch in record_asset_last_queried_feature_epoch, so it is not a dependable staleness signal on its own. For records Infoblox considers stale, use the Stale finding category in indicator_ids_str instead.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecordsRolledByIndicatorId.record_asset_last_queried_str
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Rolled by Indicator ID Record Asset Last Queried Str
dimensions.description: Formatted last-queried time, blank where record_asset_last_queried sits at the 1970 epoch. Use for display; use record_asset_last_queried for date filtering.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecordsRolledByIndicatorId.record_asset_source_str
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Rolled by Indicator ID Record Asset Source Str
dimensions.description: Comma-separated indication of how the record was created, with values such as STATIC for records created by hand or via the API, DYNAMIC for DDNS registrations, SYSTEM, DELEGATED and DTC. Use contains rather than equals. The set present is data-dependent, so group by this dimension before filtering on a value.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecordsRolledByIndicatorId.record_asset_provider_types_str
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Rolled by Indicator ID Record Asset Provider Types Str
dimensions.description: Comma-separated display names of the platforms hosting the record, with values such as AWS, GCP, Azure, NIOS-X for on-premises Infoblox DDI, and NIOS. Use contains rather than equals, since a record can carry more than one. The set present is data-dependent, so group by this dimension before filtering on a value.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecordsRolledByIndicatorId.composite_text
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Rolled by Indicator ID Composite Text
dimensions.description: A concatenation of the record's indicator, name, type, data, providers, zone and last-queried value, for keyword search across all of them. Not useful as a group-by, since it is distinct per row.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecordsRolledByIndicatorId.record_asset_ttl
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Rolled by Indicator ID Record Asset Ttl
dimensions.description: The TTL (time-to-live) value in seconds for the DNS record. Determines how long resolvers cache this record. Use when filtering by TTL or finding records with unusually high or low TTL values.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecordsRolledByIndicatorId.record_asset_tags_str
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Rolled by Indicator ID Record Asset Tags Str
dimensions.description: Tags associated with the DNS record as comma-separated key-value pairs. Use when filtering or searching records by custom metadata labels. For raw tag map access, use record_asset_tags instead.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecordsRolledByIndicatorId.record_asset_dns_rdata
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Rolled by Indicator ID Record Asset Dns Rdata
dimensions.description: The DNS protocol textual representation of the record data (wire-format). The actual DNS answer content as it would appear in a DNS response. Use when inspecting DNS response data. For JSON-structured record data, use record_asset_rdata instead.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecordsRolledByIndicatorId.synthetic_monitor_ts
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Rolled by Indicator ID Synthetic Monitor Ts
dimensions.description: An alias of evaluation_time provided for monitoring dashboards. For ordinary time filtering and bucketing use evaluation_day_ts.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecordsRolledByIndicatorId.record_asset_last_queried_feature_epoch
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Rolled by Indicator ID Record Asset Last Queried Feature Epoch
dimensions.description: When last-queried tracking was enabled for the tenant. A lookup before this point is indistinguishable from never having been queried.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecordsRolledByIndicatorId.record_asset_zone_id
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Rolled by Indicator ID Record Asset Zone ID
dimensions.description: The zone's identifier. Distinct zone identifiers can outnumber distinct zone names, because the same zone name can exist in more than one DNS view. Group by record_asset_absolute_zone_name for a zone breakdown by name.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecordsRolledByIndicatorId.indicator_ids_str
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Records Rolled by Indicator ID Indicator IDs Str
dimensions.description: The COMPLETE set of finding categories that apply to this DNS record, with readable values such as Stale, Dangling and Untrusted. This is the dimension to group by for a finding breakdown and the only one that can filter records by category correctly. Values are stored as a bracketed list whose entries are separated by a comma with NO space after it, for example ['Dangling','Untrusted']. Filter it with contains and never with equals: equals on a bare category name matches nothing, and equals on the bracketed form misses every record that carries more than one category. To find the records that carry MORE THAN ONE category, use contains on a single comma character; a comma followed by a space matches nothing. Group by it before filtering on a value, since the set present is data-dependent.

measures.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecordsRolledByIndicatorId.count
measures.title: Network Insights Dns Records Rolled by Indicator ID Count
measures.description: Number of DNS RECORDS with at least one finding, each counted once however many findings it carries. Use for how many records are affected. For a total number of individual findings, use count in NetworkInsightsDnsRecords.

measures.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecordsRolledByIndicatorId.count_uniq
measures.title: Network Insights Dns Records Rolled by Indicator ID Count Uniq
measures.description: Number of distinct DNS records with at least one finding. Identical to count on this cube, which already holds one row per record.

meta.description: Number of distinct DNS records with at least one finding. Identical to count on this cube, which already holds one row per record.

measures.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecordsRolledByIndicatorId.count_occurrences
measures.title: Network Insights Dns Records Rolled by Indicator ID Count Occurrences
measures.description: Does NOT count record-and-indicator pairs on this cube, despite its name: only one indicator survives per record here, so it returns the record count like count and count_uniq. For a genuine per-finding total, use count or count_occurrences in NetworkInsightsDnsRecords.

measures.name: NetworkInsightsDnsRecordsRolledByIndicatorId.count_zones

full.name: NetworkInsightsDnsViewLookup
full.title: Network Insights Dns View Lookup
full.description: Maps a DNS view's opaque identifier to its administrator-assigned name, one row per view. NOT AN INVENTORY OF CONFIGURED VIEWS: rows appear only for views observed carrying DNS traffic in roughly the last day, so this list can be much shorter than the account's configured views and can also contain the literal '_default', which is not a configured view object. For what is configured, and for anything about how a view is set up - the zones it serves, its client-match criteria, its IP spaces - use the DnsConfig service /dns/view and /dns/auth_zone endpoints; none of that is in this cube. This cube has NO MEASURES of any kind: pass an empty measures list and read the answer from the dimensions, and count DNS views by counting rows. It is a CURRENT SNAPSHOT, not a history: the SQL keeps one row per view, so grouping by day yields a single bucket and no trend over time can be produced here. It carries no query counts, no response codes and no client detail; for total DNS query volume per view use NstarDnsActivity (dimension dns_view, measure total_query_count) and for failed-query volume per view use NetworkInsightsDnsRawLogs. Unlike NetworkInsightsDnsRawLogs, whose source is restricted to failed responses, this cube is built from all DNS transactions, so its coverage caveats do not apply here.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsViewLookup.view_id
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns View Lookup View ID
dimensions.description: The DNS view's identifier, stored as a BARE UUID such as 8651d219-912b-4c9b-8ae4-c4e2d3f839ac, or the literal '_default'. NetworkInsightsDnsRawLogs.view_id and NstarDnsActivity.dns_view use the same bare form and join to it directly. The DnsConfig service is different: its /dns/view id field is a prefixed resource path of the form dns/view/<uuid>, so strip the dns/view/ prefix before joining REST results to this cube or the match silently returns nothing and every configured view looks inactive. Exactly one row exists per identifier.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsViewLookup.view_name
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns View Lookup View Name
dimensions.description: The administrator-assigned name of the DNS view, taken as-is from the DNS traffic record and not filled in from configuration, so it can be an empty string for a view that has no configured name. The set operator does NOT exclude those empty values; use notEquals with an empty string to drop them. The contains operator works for substring matching and is case-insensitive.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsViewLookup.timestamp
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns View Lookup Timestamp
dimensions.description: The time this DNS view was last seen carrying DNS traffic. It is the event time reported by the DNS source, not a metadata refresh time and not an ingest time, and because it is a source clock it can read slightly AHEAD of the present. Two consequences. Order by it descending to answer when a view was last active - that is what this field is for. And do NOT bound a query with a time range on it: a range whose upper bound is the present drops any view whose clock runs ahead, and a 'last N days' range returns nothing at all, while omitting the time range entirely returns every view the cube holds. There is no history on this field: only the newest record per view is kept.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsZoneLookup.zone_id
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Zone Lookup Zone ID

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsZoneLookup.zone_name
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Zone Lookup Zone Name

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsZoneLookup.timestamp
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Zone Lookup Timestamp

full.name: NetworkInsightsDnsZoneLookup
full.title: Network Insights Dns Zone Lookup
full.description: Maps a DNS zone's opaque identifier to its fully qualified domain name, one row per zone. NOT AN INVENTORY OF CONFIGURED ZONES: rows appear only for zones named in an observed DNS query within roughly the last day, so this list can be a small fraction of the account's configured zones and a row count here is NOT the account's zone count. For how many DNS zones exist, and for anything about how a zone is set up, use the DnsConfig service /dns/auth_zone and /dns/forward_zone endpoints, or TokenUtilManagementObjectsDaily with object_sub_type 'DNS Zones' for a per-day configured count. This cube also BLENDS zone kinds it cannot distinguish: an identifier here can belong to an authoritative zone or to a forward zone, with no dimension saying which, and reverse in-addr.arpa zones sit in the same list as forward ones. This cube has NO MEASURES of any kind: pass an empty measures list and read the answer from the dimensions, counting rows rather than looking for a count measure. It is a CURRENT SNAPSHOT, not a history: the SQL keeps only the newest record per zone, so grouping by day cannot yield a trend and no zone-count history can be produced here. It carries no query counts, no response codes, no record inventory and no client detail. For DNS failures broken down by zone use NetworkInsightsDnsRawLogs, which counts FAILED responses only; total DNS query volume per zone is not available through this interface. For per-zone record data use NetworkInsightsDnsRecords. For DNS host name lookups use NetworkInsightsDnsHostLookup and for DNS view name lookups use NetworkInsightsDnsViewLookup.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsZoneLookup.zone_id
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Zone Lookup Zone ID
dimensions.description: The DNS zone's identifier, stored as a BARE UUID with no prefix, in the standard hyphenated 8-4-4-4-12 form. NetworkInsightsDnsRawLogs.zone_id uses the same bare form and joins to it directly. The DnsConfig service is different: its ids are prefixed resource paths of the form dns/auth_zone/<uuid> or dns/forward_zone/<uuid>, so strip everything up to and including the last slash before joining REST results to this cube, or the match silently returns nothing and every configured zone looks inactive. An identifier here can belong to either an auth_zone or a forward_zone object, so a lookup that checks only auth_zone can fail to resolve some of them. Exactly one row exists per identifier.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsZoneLookup.zone_name
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Zone Lookup Zone Name
dimensions.description: The fully qualified domain name of the DNS zone. It is stored WITH A TRAILING DOT, as in infoblox.com., so an equals filter on a bare name that a user typed silently matches nothing; prefer contains, which is case-insensitive, or add the trailing dot to an equals value. startsWith, endsWith and notContains also work; the regex operator is NOT supported and returns an error. Reverse zones appear here under their in-addr.arpa names rather than as IP ranges. The value is taken from the DNS traffic record and defaulted to an empty string when absent, so it can be empty; the set operator does NOT exclude those, so use notEquals with an empty string to drop them.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsDnsZoneLookup.timestamp
dimensions.title: Network Insights Dns Zone Lookup Timestamp
dimensions.description: The time this DNS zone was last named in an observed DNS query. It is the event time reported by the DNS source, NOT a metadata refresh time and not an ingest time, so it tracks query traffic rather than configuration changes. Whole-second precision, so two zones last queried in the same second share a value. Because it is a source clock it can read slightly AHEAD of the present. Three consequences. Order by it descending to answer when a zone was last active, which is what this field is for. Do NOT bound a query with a time range on it: a range whose upper bound is the present drops any zone whose clock runs ahead, and a relative 'last N days' range returns the same partial subset whatever N is, while omitting the time range entirely returns every zone the cube holds. And there is no history on this field: only the newest record per zone is kept, so a day-by-day grouping reflects when zones were last queried, not how a zone count changed.

full.name: NetworkInsightsOverlappingBlocksBase
full.title: Network Insights Overlapping Blocks Base
full.description: Per-object rows for cross-IP-space IP address overlap detection: one row per overlapping object per shared address CIDR per IP space. In each row the object being described is the one whose CIDR is overlap_address; the `address` field is the shared range that object sits inside, and it is the key the overlap group is formed on. Holds only about the last day of detections and no history at all, so no trend or change-over-time question can be answered here, and queries should carry no date range: any window narrower than the cube's own span silently returns only part of the current state. Detection is change-driven rather than an inventory sweep: an object is re-evaluated only when its address changes or when it is re-synced, so this cube can hold far fewer overlaps than exist in the IP address management data. Use NetworkInsightsOverlappingBlocksList to count the blocks and subnets involved, and NetworkInsightsOverlappingBlocksRolled for a per-shared-range summary; this cube's only measure counts shared ranges, not objects.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsOverlappingBlocksBase.account_id
dimensions.title: Network Insights Overlapping Blocks Base Account ID
dimensions.description: Internal tenant identifier for the customer's CSP account, automatically filtered by the platform's security context. Primary key for row uniqueness. Use when filtering or grouping overlapping blocks by tenant account.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsOverlappingBlocksBase.insert_time
dimensions.title: Network Insights Overlapping Blocks Base Insert Time
dimensions.description: When the overlap detection pipeline recorded this row, set from the refresh clock rather than from any property of the object. Only about the last day is retained. When a query needs a date range, use this dimension. But prefer no time dimension at all: each object is represented by a single row carrying whatever time the detector last touched it, and those times are spread across the cube's whole window, so ANY narrower window returns only the objects refreshed inside it. A one-hour window can return almost nothing on an account with many overlaps, and a 24-hour window returns well under the full set, with the shortfall growing through the day. Grouping by day splits the one snapshot across at most two calendar buckets whose difference is a refresh artifact rather than a change in the data, so sum the buckets and never compare them.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsOverlappingBlocksBase.address
dimensions.title: Network Insights Overlapping Blocks Base Address
dimensions.description: The shared IP range that this overlap group is keyed on, in CIDR form. It is the CIDR of the counterpart, not of the object this row describes: many rows share one `address` value, each describing a different object nested inside it. Group by this to see which ranges are contested. For the CIDR of the object named in this row, use overlap_address.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsOverlappingBlocksBase.overlap_address
dimensions.title: Network Insights Overlapping Blocks Base Overlap Address
dimensions.description: The CIDR of the object this row actually describes, the one named by ref_name and typed by type_pretty. It sits inside the shared range in `address`. Project this whenever you list or name individual overlapping objects; attaching ref_name to `address` instead labels one object's name onto a whole shared range.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsOverlappingBlocksBase.id_resource_id
dimensions.title: Network Insights Overlapping Blocks Base ID Resource ID
dimensions.description: Unique resource identifier of the primary overlapping object (address block or subnet). Primary key for row uniqueness. Use when looking up a specific overlapping object by ID. For the counterpart's ID, use overlap_id_resource_id.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsOverlappingBlocksBase.overlap_id_resource_id
dimensions.title: Network Insights Overlapping Blocks Base Overlap ID Resource ID
dimensions.description: An alias of id_resource_id, backed by the same column. The counterpart object's identifier is not present in this data.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsOverlappingBlocksBase.id_resource_type
dimensions.title: Network Insights Overlapping Blocks Base ID Resource Type
dimensions.description: Resource type of the overlapping object: 'address_block' or 'subnet'. Equivalent to the type dimension. Use when filtering overlaps by raw object type. For display-friendly labels, use type_pretty instead.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsOverlappingBlocksBase.id_application_name
dimensions.title: Network Insights Overlapping Blocks Base ID Application Name
dimensions.description: Application identifier for the overlapping object. Use when filtering overlaps by the originating application or grouping by application name.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsOverlappingBlocksBase.space_id_resource_id
dimensions.title: Network Insights Overlapping Blocks Base Space ID Resource ID
dimensions.description: Unique resource identifier of the IP space containing this object. Use when filtering overlaps by IP space or looking up objects within a specific IP space.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsOverlappingBlocksBase.space_id_resource_type
dimensions.title: Network Insights Overlapping Blocks Base Space ID Resource Type
dimensions.description: Resource type of the IP space containing this object. Use when filtering overlaps by IP space resource type.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsOverlappingBlocksBase.space_id_application_name
dimensions.title: Network Insights Overlapping Blocks Base Space ID Application Name
dimensions.description: Application identifier for the IP space containing this object. Use when filtering overlaps by the IP space's originating application.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsOverlappingBlocksBase.space_name
dimensions.title: Network Insights Overlapping Blocks Base Space Name
dimensions.description: Name of the IP space containing the primary overlapping object. Use when grouping or filtering overlaps by IP space name. For the counterpart's IP space name, use overlap_space_name instead.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsOverlappingBlocksBase.overlap_space_name
dimensions.title: Network Insights Overlapping Blocks Base Overlap Space Name
dimensions.description: An alias of space_name, backed by the same column, so a filter comparing the two can never distinguish them. The counterpart object's IP space is not present in this data.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsOverlappingBlocksBase.ref_name
dimensions.title: Network Insights Overlapping Blocks Base Ref Name
dimensions.description: Name of the object this row describes, the one whose CIDR is overlap_address. It can be an empty string for objects that carry no name upstream. Those blanks are empty strings rather than nulls, so the null-based operators do not see them: `set` matches named and unnamed objects alike, and `notSet` matches nothing at all and reads as though every object is named. Use notEquals with an empty value to restrict to named objects, and equals with an empty value to find the unnamed ones.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsOverlappingBlocksBase.overlap_name
dimensions.title: Network Insights Overlapping Blocks Base Overlap Name
dimensions.description: An alias of ref_name, backed by the same column, so it always carries the same value and is empty on exactly the same rows. The counterpart object's name is not present in this data at all. To see what an object conflicts with, group the rows that share one `address` value. The same empty-string caveat as ref_name applies: `notSet` matches nothing here.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsOverlappingBlocksBase.source
dimensions.title: Network Insights Overlapping Blocks Base Source
dimensions.description: Where the object this row describes was discovered. Values take the form `On-Prem` and `Cloud`; the form `On-Premise` does not occur. Group by this dimension before filtering on a literal.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsOverlappingBlocksBase.provider
dimensions.title: Network Insights Overlapping Blocks Base Provider
dimensions.description: Raw provider identifier for the overlapping object. Use when filtering by exact provider value or programmatic matching. Prefer provider_pretty for display-friendly provider names.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsOverlappingBlocksBase.provider_pretty

full.name: NetworkInsightsOverlappingBlocksList
full.title: Network Insights Overlapping Blocks List
full.description: Deduplicated inventory of the address blocks and subnets involved in cross-IP-space IP overlaps, one row per object per IP space. This is the cube that answers 'how many of my blocks and subnets are overlapping' and 'list the overlapping objects': its count and overlap_count measures are the only ones in this family that count objects. In each row the object being described is the one whose CIDR is overlap_address; the `address` field is the shared range that object sits inside. Holds only about the last day of detections and no history, so no trend question can be answered here, and queries should carry no date range: any window narrower than the cube's own span silently returns only part of the current count. Detection is change-driven rather than an inventory sweep, so this cube can hold far fewer overlaps than exist in the IP address management data. Utilisation, DHCP settings, tags, comments and access views are not carried here; those live on the IPAM subnet and address block collections. For a per-shared-range summary use NetworkInsightsOverlappingBlocksRolled.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsOverlappingBlocksList.account_id
dimensions.title: Network Insights Overlapping Blocks List Account ID
dimensions.description: Internal tenant identifier for the customer's CSP account, automatically filtered by the platform's security context. Primary key for row uniqueness. Use when filtering or grouping overlapping blocks by tenant account.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsOverlappingBlocksList.insert_time
dimensions.title: Network Insights Overlapping Blocks List Insert Time
dimensions.description: When the overlap detection pipeline recorded this row, set from the refresh clock rather than from any property of the object. Only about the last day is retained. When a query needs a date range, use this dimension. But prefer no time dimension at all: each object is represented by a single row carrying whatever time the detector last touched it, and those times are spread across the cube's whole window, so ANY narrower window returns only the objects refreshed inside it. A one-hour window can return almost nothing on an account with many overlaps, and a 24-hour window returns well under the full set, with the shortfall growing through the day. Grouping by day splits the one snapshot across at most two calendar buckets whose difference is a refresh artifact rather than a change in the data, so sum the buckets and never compare them.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsOverlappingBlocksList.address
dimensions.title: Network Insights Overlapping Blocks List Address
dimensions.description: The shared IP range that this overlap group is keyed on, in CIDR form. It is the CIDR of the counterpart, not of the object this row describes: many rows share one `address` value, each describing a different object nested inside it. Group by this to see which ranges are contested. For the CIDR of the object named in this row, use overlap_address.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsOverlappingBlocksList.overlap_address

dimensions.description: The CIDR of the object this row actually describes, the one named by ref_name and typed by type_pretty. It sits inside the shared range in `address`. Project this whenever you list or name individual overlapping objects; attaching ref_name to `address` instead labels one object's name onto a whole shared range.

measures.description: Number of overlapping objects, one per row of this deduplicated inventory. Use this for 'how many address blocks and subnets are involved in overlaps'. It is additive, so a breakdown by platform, type, source or IP space sums back to the total.

measures.name: NetworkInsightsOverlappingBlocksList.overlap_count
measures.title: Network Insights Overlapping Blocks List Overlap Count
measures.description: Number of distinct overlapping objects, counted as unique account, resource and IP space triples. Equivalent to count unless an object appears in more than one IP space, in which case count is the higher of the two. Either answers 'how many blocks and subnets are involved in overlaps'.

full.ai_context: An overlap needs at least two surviving objects on the same range. Rows here are detections, not live conflicts: a range can still appear here after its counterparts were deleted from IPAM, in which case it is not currently overlapping anything and must not be listed as a live overlap. Do not test for that by grouping this cube on address: the deduplication here drops address from its key, so which shared range an object keeps is arbitrary. Take the surviving-claimant count from NetworkInsightsOverlappingBlocksRolled.overlap_count, unfiltered, and treat a range whose count is 1 as a stale detection rather than an overlap.

full.name: NetworkInsightsOverlappingBlocksRolled
full.title: Network Insights Overlapping Blocks Rolled
full.description: Cross-IP-space IP overlap detection rolled up to one row per shared address range per tenant, with the number of objects claiming that range and the lists of IP spaces, discovery sources and platforms involved. It carries no per-object detail and no time dimension: there are no object names, types, providers or identifiers here, and no way to bound or bucket a query in time, so the answer is always the current snapshot covering roughly the last day of detections. For per-object detail, or for any question that needs a time range, use NetworkInsightsOverlappingBlocksList. Detection is change-driven rather than an inventory sweep, so this cube can hold far fewer overlaps than exist in the IP address management data.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsOverlappingBlocksRolled.address
dimensions.title: Network Insights Overlapping Blocks Rolled Address
dimensions.description: The shared IP range this row summarises, in CIDR form. One row per range. This is the range that more than one block or subnet is claiming.

meta.description: The shared IP range this row summarises, in CIDR form. One row per range. This is the range that more than one block or subnet is claiming.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsOverlappingBlocksRolled.overlap_count
dimensions.title: Network Insights Overlapping Blocks Rolled Overlap Count
dimensions.description: The number of distinct objects still claiming this shared range. A dimension rather than a measure, so it cannot be aggregated; project it alongside address and order by it to rank the worst overlaps. In an unfiltered query, a value of 1 means the other members of the group were dropped after the group was formed, in practice because the object had been deleted from IPAM: there is no counterpart left to name and the range is not currently overlapping anything, so do not report such a row as a live overlapping network. A providers_str or sources_str filter rewrites this figure to the objects that survived that filter, which makes live overlaps read as 1, so never apply those filters when this figure matters: query unfiltered and narrow with query_stored_data instead.

A list holding a single name does not mean one namespace overlaps itself: it means only one claimant survives, so read an unfiltered overlap_count before describing the row as an overlap.

In an unfiltered query, overlap_count = 1 means no counterpart survives: the other claimants were dropped after the overlap group was formed (in every case root-caused so far, because the object had been deleted from IPAM), and on some tenants most rows are of this kind. Do not present such a row as a live overlapping network, and do not read its one-element space_names_str as a namespace overlapping itself: exclude those rows and say how many you excluded, or list them separately as stale detections whose counterpart no longer exists. Those two are pushed into the pre-aggregation and rewrite overlap_count to the filtered subset, so a live overlap reports 1 there and the test silently deletes it. To scope an answer to one provider or source, query this cube unfiltered and narrow the rows afterwards with query_stored_data.

full.name: NetworkInsightsSubnet
full.title: Network Insights Subnet
full.description: IP subnets (IPv4 and IPv6) within IP spaces. One row per subnet PER IP SPACE, holding only the latest state, so the same CIDR can legitimately appear many times. Use for subnet inventory, per-subnet IP utilization, DHCP status, provider breakdown and federated realm membership. Deleted subnets are absent. For utilization trends over time use NetworkInsightsSubnetUtilization; for ranges that overlap across IP spaces use the NetworkInsightsOverlappingBlocks cubes.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsSubnet.account_id
dimensions.title: Network Insights Subnet Account ID
dimensions.description: Internal tenant identifier for the customer's CSP account, auto-filtered by the platform's security context. Use when grouping subnets by tenant account.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsSubnet.ref_id_application_name
dimensions.title: Network Insights Subnet Ref ID Application Name
dimensions.description: The application identifier for the subnet resource. Use when filtering by the originating application. For the subnet's display name, use name. For the unique ID, use ref_id_resource_id.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsSubnet.ref_id_resource_type
dimensions.title: Network Insights Subnet Ref ID Resource Type
dimensions.description: The application-specific type name of the subnet resource. Use when filtering by resource type. For the subnet's display name, use name. For the unique ID, use ref_id_resource_id.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsSubnet.ref_id_resource_id
dimensions.title: Network Insights Subnet Ref ID Resource ID
dimensions.description: The unique resource identity of the subnet. Use when looking up a specific subnet by its ID. For the subnet's display name, use name instead.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsSubnet.name
dimensions.title: Network Insights Subnet Name
dimensions.description: The administrator-assigned name of the subnet. Can be unset, and an unset name is stored as an EMPTY STRING rather than null, so `set`/`notSet` do not distinguish it - test with `equals ""` or `notEquals ""`. Because a subnet may have no name, prefer `address` plus `space_name` when identifying one.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsSubnet.address
dimensions.title: Network Insights Subnet Address
dimensions.description: The subnet in CIDR notation, for example 192.168.1.0/24. This is NOT unique: the same CIDR can exist in many IP spaces at once, so a filter on it can return many subnets. Pair it with `space_name` to identify one subnet, and use `ref_id_resource_id` when a single unambiguous key is needed. For just the prefix length use `cidr`.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsSubnet.cidr
dimensions.title: Network Insights Subnet Cidr
dimensions.description: The CIDR prefix length of the subnet (e.g., 24 for a /24). Use when filtering by subnet size or prefix length. For the full CIDR notation including the network address, use address.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsSubnet.protocol
dimensions.title: Network Insights Subnet Protocol
dimensions.description: The IP protocol version, ip4 for IPv4 or ip6 for IPv6. Use when filtering subnets by protocol or comparing IPv4 vs. IPv6 inventory. Also determines which utilization values apply to protocol-aware combined fields.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsSubnet.comment
dimensions.title: Network Insights Subnet Comment
dimensions.description: User-provided description for the subnet (0-1024 characters, UTF-8). Use when searching subnets by their description or notes. For custom metadata labels, use tags instead.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsSubnet.space_id_application_name
dimensions.title: Network Insights Subnet Space ID Application Name
dimensions.description: The application identifier for the IP space containing this subnet. Use when filtering by the IP space's originating application. For the space display name, use space_name.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsSubnet.space_id_resource_type
dimensions.title: Network Insights Subnet Space ID Resource Type
dimensions.description: The resource type of the IP space containing this subnet. Use when filtering by IP space resource type. For the space display name, use space_name.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsSubnet.space_id_resource_id
dimensions.title: Network Insights Subnet Space ID Resource ID
dimensions.description: The unique resource identity of the IP space containing this subnet. Use when querying subnets within a specific IP space by ID. For the display name, use space_name.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsSubnet.space_name
dimensions.title: Network Insights Subnet Space Name
dimensions.description: The name of the IP space containing this subnet. Use when grouping or filtering subnets by IP space. For the unique IP space ID, use space_id_resource_id instead.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsSubnet.tags
dimensions.title: Network Insights Subnet Tags
dimensions.description: Tags on the subnet, rendered as `'key':'value'` pairs separated by commas. Key order is not stable, so identical tag sets can appear as different strings and a group-by will split them; match a single tag with `contains`. For network discovery data use `discovery_metadata` or `discovery_attrs` instead.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsSubnet.disable_dhcp
dimensions.title: Network Insights Subnet Disable Dhcp
dimensions.description: Whether DHCP is disabled for this subnet (true = disabled). Use when filtering for DHCP-active vs. DHCP-disabled subnets or checking DHCP status.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsSubnet.dhcp_host_id_application_name
dimensions.title: Network Insights Subnet Dhcp Host ID Application Name
dimensions.description: The application identifier of the DHCP host or HA group serving this subnet. Use when filtering by DHCP host application. For the host name, use service_instance. For the HA group name, use ha_group.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsSubnet.dhcp_host_id_resource_type
dimensions.title: Network Insights Subnet Dhcp Host ID Resource Type
dimensions.description: The resource type of the DHCP host or HA group serving this subnet. The values are `host` and `ha_group`, with no `dhcp/` prefix, and the field is empty when no DHCP host is assigned. For host names use `service_instance`; for group names use `ha_group`.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsSubnet.dhcp_host_id_resource_id
dimensions.title: Network Insights Subnet Dhcp Host ID Resource ID
dimensions.description: The unique resource identity of the DHCP host or HA group serving this subnet. Use when looking up subnets served by a specific DHCP host by ID. For the host name, use service_instance.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsSubnet.service_instance
dimensions.title: Network Insights Subnet Service Instance
dimensions.description: The name of the DHCP service instance associated with the subnet. Only populated when the DHCP host is a standalone host (dhcp/host). Use when filtering or grouping subnets by DHCP server. For HA group names, use ha_group instead.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsSubnet.ha_group
dimensions.title: Network Insights Subnet Ha Group
dimensions.description: The name of the HA (high availability) group associated with the subnet. Only populated when the DHCP host is an HA group (dhcp/ha_group). Use when filtering subnets by HA group. For standalone host names, use service_instance instead.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsSubnet.source
dimensions.title: Network Insights Subnet Source
dimensions.description: The deployment model of the subnet. The only two values are `On-Prem` and `Cloud` - note `On-Prem`, not `On-Premise`, which matches nothing. For the specific cloud or DDI vendor use `provider` instead.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsSubnet.provider
dimensions.title: Network Insights Subnet Provider
dimensions.description: The cloud or DDI provider name. Values: AWS, GCP, Azure, NIOS-X, NIOS. Use when filtering or grouping subnets by provider, e.g., 'show all AWS subnets' or 'compare utilization across providers.' For deployment model (On-Premise vs Cloud), use source instead.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsSubnet.access_view_id
dimensions.title: Network Insights Subnet Access View ID
dimensions.description: The reference ID of the access view associated with the subnet. Use when looking up a specific access view by ID. For the display name, use access_view_name instead.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsSubnet.access_view_name
dimensions.title: Network Insights Subnet Access View Name
dimensions.description: The name of the access view associated with the subnet; defaults to 'Unassigned' if none is set. Use when grouping or filtering subnets by access view. For ID-based lookups, use access_view_id.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsSubnet.utilization_total
dimensions.title: Network Insights Subnet Utilization Total
dimensions.description: Total number of IPv4 addresses in the subnet. Zero on every IPv6 subnet, which has no IPv4 total, so an estate-wide IPv4 capacity or free-space figure computed without filtering by protocol silently includes those zeros; filter to `protocol == 'ip4'` first. For the IPv6 total use `utilization_v6_total`.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsSubnet.utilization_used
dimensions.title: Network Insights Subnet Utilization Used
dimensions.description: Number of IPv4 addresses currently used in the subnet. Use when checking how many IPv4 IPs are consumed. For IPv6 used count, use utilization_v6_used. For combined utilization percentage, use utilization_percent.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsSubnet.utilization_free
dimensions.title: Network Insights Subnet Utilization Free
dimensions.description: Number of free (available) IPv4 addresses in the subnet. Use when checking remaining IPv4 capacity or finding subnets with available space. For a protocol-aware free count, use utilization_free_combined.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsSubnet.utilization_utilization
dimensions.title: Network Insights Subnet Utilization Utilization
dimensions.description: Percentage of used IPv4 addresses relative to the IPv4 total. Stored as a whole number, so it is truncated to the integer and any subnet below one percent reads as 0. Zero on IPv6 subnets, which have no IPv4 total. For the combined figure use `utilization_percent`; for a bucketed tier use `percentage_bucket`.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsSubnet.utilization_abandoned
dimensions.title: Network Insights Subnet Utilization Abandoned
dimensions.description: Number of IPv4 addresses in the abandoned state (issued by DHCP then declined by client). Use when detecting abandoned lease issues in the subnet. For IPv6 abandoned count, use utilization_v6_abandoned. For the abandon percentage, use utilization_abandon_utilization.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsSubnet.utilization_abandon_utilization
dimensions.title: Network Insights Subnet Utilization Abandon Utilization
dimensions.description: Percentage of abandoned IPv4 addresses relative to total in the subnet. Use when measuring the severity of abandoned lease problems. For the raw abandoned count, use utilization_abandoned. For overall used percentage, use utilization_utilization.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsSubnet.utilization_dynamic
dimensions.title: Network Insights Subnet Utilization Dynamic
dimensions.description: Number of IPv4 addresses handed out by DHCP (leases, fixed addresses, abandoned leases). Use when checking IPv4 DHCP-assigned allocation counts. For IPv6 dynamic count, use utilization_v6_dynamic. For a protocol-aware DHCP count, use utilization_dhcp_combined.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsSubnet.utilization_static
dimensions.title: Network Insights Subnet Utilization Static
dimensions.description: Number of statically defined IPv4 addresses (reservations, DNS records). Computed as used minus dynamic. Use when checking how many IPv4 IPs are reserved. For IPv6 static count, use utilization_v6_static. For a protocol-aware static count, use utilization_static_combined.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsSubnet.utilization_v6_total
dimensions.title: Network Insights Subnet Utilization V6 Total
dimensions.description: Total number of IPv6 addresses available in the subnet. Use when checking IPv6 subnet capacity. For IPv4 total, use utilization_total.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsSubnet.utilization_v6_used
dimensions.title: Network Insights Subnet Utilization V6 Used
dimensions.description: Number of IPv6 addresses currently used in the subnet. Use when checking IPv6 consumption. For IPv4 used count, use utilization_used.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsSubnet.utilization_v6_static
dimensions.title: Network Insights Subnet Utilization V6 Static
dimensions.description: Number of statically defined IPv6 addresses (reservations, DNS records). Use when checking how many IPv6 IPs are reserved. For IPv4 static count, use utilization_static. For a protocol-aware static count, use utilization_static_combined.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsSubnet.utilization_v6_dynamic
dimensions.title: Network Insights Subnet Utilization V6 Dynamic
dimensions.description: Number of IPv6 addresses handed out by DHCP. Use when checking IPv6 DHCP allocation counts. For IPv4 dynamic count, use utilization_dynamic. For a protocol-aware DHCP count, use utilization_dhcp_combined.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsSubnet.utilization_v6_abandoned
dimensions.title: Network Insights Subnet Utilization V6 Abandoned
dimensions.description: Number of IPv6 addresses in the abandoned state. Use when detecting IPv6 abandoned lease issues. For IPv4 abandoned count, use utilization_abandoned.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsSubnet.utilization_static_combined
dimensions.title: Network Insights Subnet Utilization Static Combined
dimensions.description: Count of statically defined IP addresses in the subnet; auto-selects IPv4 or IPv6 based on protocol. Use when querying reserved or statically assigned IPs regardless of protocol. For IPv4-specific, use utilization_static. For IPv6-specific, use utilization_v6_static.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsSubnet.utilization_free_combined
dimensions.title: Network Insights Subnet Utilization Free Combined
dimensions.description: Count of free (available, unused) IP addresses in the subnet; auto-selects IPv4 or IPv6 based on protocol. Use when checking available capacity regardless of protocol. For IPv4-specific free count, use utilization_free.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsSubnet.utilization_dhcp_combined
dimensions.title: Network Insights Subnet Utilization Dhcp Combined
dimensions.description: Count of DHCP-assigned IP addresses in the subnet; auto-selects IPv4 or IPv6 based on protocol. Use when querying DHCP usage regardless of protocol. For IPv4-specific, use utilization_dynamic. For IPv6-specific, use utilization_v6_dynamic.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsSubnet.usage
dimensions.title: Network Insights Subnet Usage
dimensions.description: Usage indicators for the subnet, as a single comma-separated string joining every indicator that applies, for example `IPAM`, `DISCOVERED, IPAM` or `DISCOVERED, IPAM, DHCP`. The individual indicators are IPAM (managed in the DDI product), DHCP (served by a DHCP host) and DISCOVERED (found by Network Insight or NetMRI). Because the values are combinations, match with `contains`; `equals` on a single indicator silently misses every combined row and can return zero. The set of combinations present is data-dependent, so group by this dimension before filtering.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsSubnet.discovery_metadata
dimensions.title: Network Insights Subnet Discovery Metadata
dimensions.description: Discovery metadata for the subnet as comma-separated key-value pairs. Use when filtering or searching subnets by network discovery metadata. For custom administrator labels, use tags. For discovery attributes, use discovery_attrs.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsSubnet.discovery_attrs
dimensions.title: Network Insights Subnet Discovery Attrs
dimensions.description: Discovery attributes for the subnet as comma-separated key-value pairs. Use when filtering or searching subnets by network discovery attributes. For custom administrator labels, use tags. For discovery metadata, use discovery_metadata.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsSubnet.federated_realms
dimensions.title: Network Insights Subnet Federated Realms
dimensions.description: Names of the federated realms this subnet participates in, joined with a comma and NO space, and empty when the subnet is in none. The element order is not stable, so the same set of realms can appear as two different strings and a plain group-by will split it and understate each realm. To count subnets per realm, filter with `contains` on one realm name at a time.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsSubnet.created_at
dimensions.title: Network Insights Subnet Created at
dimensions.description: Timestamp when the subnet was created. Spans the full history of the account and is not limited by the snapshot window, reaching back years. A time range on this field is capped at 400 days, so to find the oldest subnets query it as an ordinary dimension ordered ascending rather than as a time dimension with a wide range. For last modification use `updated_at`.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsSubnet.updated_at
dimensions.title: Network Insights Subnet Updated at
dimensions.description: Timestamp when the subnet was last updated; equals `created_at` if never modified. Honours a time range, capped at 400 days like `created_at`. This is the only way to ask when a subnet last changed: the cube carries no separate ingest-time or snapshot-time field that can be queried.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsSubnet.percentage_bucket
dimensions.title: Network Insights Subnet Percentage Bucket
dimensions.description: Utilization tier: 0-20%, 20-40%, 40-60%, 60-80%, 80-100%, or `unknown` when the subnet has no capacity at all. Derived from `utilization_percent`, so IPv6 subnets with large prefixes are pushed into the lowest bucket regardless of real usage, which inflates that bucket. Filter to `protocol == 'ip4'` for a distribution that can be read at face value.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsSubnet.utilization_percent
dimensions.title: Network Insights Subnet Utilization Percent
dimensions.description: Percentage of used addresses out of the total, combining IPv4 and IPv6. Meaningful for IPv4 subnets, but NOT comparable for an IPv6 subnet with a large prefix: the denominator is the entire IPv6 address space of that prefix, so the result collapses to a value indistinguishable from zero however many addresses are in use. When comparing utilization across protocols, report IPv4 and IPv6 separately using their own used and total fields. For a bucketed tier use `percentage_bucket`, which inherits the same IPv6 caveat.

measures.name: NetworkInsightsSubnet.count
measures.title: Network Insights Subnet Count
measures.description: Number of subnet rows matching the filters, counting one row per subnet per IP space. This is the ONLY measure on this cube: there is no sum or average of used, free or total addresses, and putting a utilization dimension in `measures` fails. Because `address` is not unique, this counts subnets rather than distinct network ranges.

full.ai_context: Every row is the CURRENT state of a subnet, captured in a single refresh within roughly the last day; there is no ingest-time or snapshot-time field to query and no older revision to compare against. Grain is one row per subnet per IP space; `ref_id_resource_id` is the row identity and `address` is not unique. Because the cube holds one snapshot rather than history, no trend, no growth rate and no as-at-a-past-date answer can come from it: for utilization over time use NetworkInsightsSubnetUtilization, and for a subnet's own lifecycle dates use `created_at` and `updated_at`, which do span years. `count` is the only measure: every utilization field is a per-subnet dimension, so totals and averages over them are not available here and placing one in `measures` fails. Combined IPv4+IPv6 utilization percentages are not comparable across protocols, because an IPv6 prefix contributes its whole address space to the denominator. Several string fields are joined multi-value strings whose element order is not stable, so match them with `contains` rather than `equals` and treat a group-by on them as approximate. A time range is only honoured on `created_at` and `updated_at`, and is limited to 400 days.

full.name: NetworkInsightsSubnetUtilization
full.title: Network Insights Subnet Utilization
full.description: Account-wide IPv4/IPv6 address utilisation as a daily time series, one aggregate row per day, covering today plus the previous seven calendar days. This is the only source of a multi-day utilisation trend. It carries NO subnet identity, no IP space and no protocol dimension, so it cannot show, filter to, group by or rank an individual subnet, space or protocol; for any of those, and for current per-subnet state or a subnet count, use NetworkInsightsSubnet or the IPAM subnet API. A date range wider than the window is accepted without error and silently returns only the days that exist, so a longer trend cannot be produced here. The single utilisation percentage measure needs a filter to be meaningful: read its description before using it.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsSubnetUtilization.account_id
dimensions.title: Network Insights Subnet Utilization Account ID
dimensions.description: Tenant this data belongs to. Already scoped to the caller by the platform, so it is not a selector; a filter naming a different account is refused.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsSubnetUtilization.generated_at
dimensions.title: Network Insights Subnet Utilization Generated at
dimensions.description: Time the utilisation snapshot was generated by the producer, recorded to whole seconds. Align a range to midnight boundaries: rows arrive in bulk refresh bursts rather than evenly, so a daily bucket is only representative when the range covers the whole day. Values are the individual refresh timestamps rather than one per day, so a query that groups on this dimension needs an explicit day granularity to produce a daily series. The available range is today plus the previous seven calendar days. This is event time, not the time the row was loaded; load time is not available here. To answer how current the data is, read the maximum value of this dimension: it is the timestamp of the most recent snapshot and it is queryable, so a data-freshness question has a concrete answer rather than only a description of the refresh behaviour.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsSubnetUtilization.utilization_used
dimensions.title: Network Insights Subnet Utilization Utilization Used
dimensions.description: Number of IPv4 addresses in use, for one subnet on one day. This is a dimension value, not an aggregate: it cannot be summed or averaged by this cube, and placing it in measures is rejected. Summing these rows client-side does not work either, because with no subnet identity in this cube the rows deduplicate. For an account-wide total of addresses in use, use NetworkInsightsSubnet or the IPAM subnet API.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsSubnetUtilization.utilization_total
dimensions.title: Network Insights Subnet Utilization Utilization Total
dimensions.description: Number of IPv4 addresses available, for one subnet on one day. This is a dimension value, not an aggregate: it cannot be summed or averaged by this cube, and placing it in measures is rejected. Grouping on it alone returns its distinct values, which are subnet sizes rather than one row per subnet.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsSubnetUtilization.utilization_v6_used
dimensions.title: Network Insights Subnet Utilization Utilization V6 Used
dimensions.description: Number of IPv6 addresses in use, for one subnet on one day. A dimension value, not an aggregate; placing it in measures is rejected, and summing these rows client-side is unreliable because they deduplicate. For an account-wide IPv6 address count, use the IPAM address or subnet API.

dimensions.name: NetworkInsightsSubnetUtilization.utilization_v6_total
dimensions.title: Network Insights Subnet Utilization Utilization V6 Total
dimensions.description: Size of the subnet's IPv6 address space for one subnet on one day, not a count of usable addresses, and many orders of magnitude larger than any IPv4 figure. A dimension value, not an aggregate; placing it in measures is rejected. Its main practical use is as a filter: utilization_v6_total == 0 selects the subnets with no IPv6 capacity, which is what makes utilization_percentage meaningful.

measures.name: NetworkInsightsSubnetUtilization.utilization_percentage
measures.title: Network Insights Subnet Utilization Utilization Percentage
measures.description: Account-wide address utilisation percentage. TO GET A MEANINGFUL FIGURE, ALWAYS ADD THE FILTER utilization_v6_total == 0, which restricts the aggregate to subnets that have no IPv6 capacity and yields the true IPv4 utilisation. ALIGN THE DATE RANGE TO WHOLE DAYS, for example from midnight to midnight. If a range cannot be aligned, disregard its first bucket. Aggregate at a day granularity: adding generated_at to the group-by splits the aggregate down to roughly a single subnet per group and returns a plausible percentage that belongs to no identifiable subnet. Do not rebuild a total by pulling the per-subnet counters and summing them either, because with no subnet identity those rows deduplicate and the sum comes out short. Requires an explicit date range; a granularity alone is rejected. Computed as SUM(utilization_used + utilization_v6_used) / SUM(utilization_total + utilization_v6_total) * 100. THE TWO TOTALS ARE NOT THE SAME KIND OF QUANTITY: utilization_total counts IPv4 addresses, while utilization_v6_total is the size of an IPv6 address space and is many orders of magnitude larger. Added together the IPv6 term dominates the denominator, so the unfiltered measure returns a figure far below the true utilisation. A range that begins part-way through a day makes that first daily bucket cover only the subnets refreshed after that instant, and the pooled figure over that partial subset can read tens of times higher than the real one while every later bucket is correct. This is a pooled ratio, total used over total capacity, not an average of the individual subnets' percentages; because it weights by subnet size, an account of large sparsely-used subnets reads far lower than a typical individual subnet does. IPv6 consumption is not usefully expressed as a percentage at all, since the denominator is an address space rather than a supply of addresses; report IPv6 usage as a count of addresses instead.

full.ai_context: Grain: one aggregate row per day, today plus the previous seven calendar days. There is no count measure and no subnet, IP space or protocol dimension, so subnet counts, per-subnet figures, rankings and breakdowns are not answerable here and belong to NetworkInsightsSubnet or the IPAM subnet API. IMPORTANT: utilization_percentage sums IPv6 address-space sizes together with IPv4 address counts, so without the filter utilization_v6_total == 0 it returns a figure many orders of magnitude below the real one. Align any date range to whole days: a partial first day covers only part of the fleet and reads far higher than the real figure. Aggregate it at a day granularity; grouping it by the raw snapshot timestamp returns a plausible-looking percentage that belongs to no identifiable subnet. Do not attempt to rebuild a total by pulling the per-subnet counters and summing them: with no subnet identity the rows deduplicate and the sum comes out short. Only one measure exists, utilization_percentage, and it requires an explicit date range.

full.name: NetworkNstarDhcpLeaseActivity

full.description: DHCP lease activity data including lease assignments, renewals, and terminations. Captures per-lease details such as leased IP address, MAC address, client hostname, DHCP fingerprint, lease operation type, lease lifecycle timestamps (start/end), protocol (IPv4/IPv6), IP space, host and subnet context, and lease state — for comprehensive DHCP monitoring and reporting.

dimensions.name: NetworkNstarDhcpLeaseActivity.query_nanosec

dimensions.name: NetworkNstarDhcpLeaseActivity.lease_end
dimensions.title: Nstar DHCP Lease Activity (ClickHouse) Lease End

full.name: SecurityActionAssets
full.title: Security Action Assets
full.description: Per-asset detail for security actions, one row per asset per security action. Terminology: "insight" is the user-facing alias for "security action" in the IQ Threat Defense UI — treat the two terms as synonyms. Each record describes a device including network identifiers (IP, MAC, hostname), threat indicators on the asset, associated users, event counts, verification status, risk flag, provider/region, ranking, and first/last detection timeline. Scope: rows created in the last 30 days where the parent security action has visible=true and evaluation_start_date within the last 30 days (matching SecurityActionSummaryView's scope). Use this cube to check all assets involved for a particular security action, or to see all risky assets across security actions — it's suggested to use it with securityActionDisplayId in the filter when scoping to a single security action. For security action-level summaries use SecurityActionSummaryView; for indicator-level drill-downs use SecurityActionIndicators.

This is an internal identifier and should NOT be used for filtering — if a filter on security action ID is required, filter on securityActionDisplayId instead. Use securityActionId only for joining to security action-level data.

dimensions.description: Cross-source device identifier (e.g. "cq-9b3c7e1a-...") used to correlate this asset across asset-inventory data sources. Use for tracking a specific device across security actions or joining to external inventory.
